Decide who may enter your defended circle during a siege when the Citadel cannot safely shelter everyone at once.
Recover the shattered seal of a prior Citadel bearer to learn how an apparently absolute defense was once breached.

name: Divine Artifact Bond
summary: A relic-lineage Authority that fuses legitimacy, growth, and command to a single artifact-grade instrument.
description: Divine Artifact Bond is an Authority that fuses the bearer's legitimacy and growth to a single relic-grade artifact. It belongs in the Authority category because the core fantasy is recognized dominion through bond and inheritance, not a sprawling self-contained System. The artifact is not just gear, but a co-sovereign instrument whose awakening stages redefine what kinds of command the bearer can exercise. Its progression bias favors loyalty, synchronized growth, and singular mastery over broad equipment flexibility. The main tradeoff is dependence, because losing, damaging, corrupting, or politically contesting the bonded artifact threatens the bearer's standing and combat identity at once. In the world, Divine Artifact Bond attracts worshippers, thieves, bureaucrats, historians, and rival claimants because any relic this important sits inside a chain of legitimacy older than the current wielder. It also creates questions of succession and personhood, since the bearer may be judged less as an individual and more as the present voice of the artifact's line. It remains lore-safe because the bond grants authority through a bounded relic lineage, not through direct supremacy over the whole cosmic order, and because the artifact itself can refuse, sleep, fracture, or demand terms.
coreLoop: Deepen the bond with a single relic-grade artifact through deeds, resonance, and mutual recognition rather than treating it as replaceable equipment.
Feed the artifact essence, oaths, and achievement so its dormant authority states can awaken in sequence.
Learn to wield the bond as a shared command structure where bearer and artifact each shape what the other can become.
Trigger Divine Artifact Bond's authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression grants basic resonance, unique techniques, and the first signs that the artifact is more sovereign partner than tool.
Mid progression awakens relic states, inherited laws, and stricter terms governing who may wield, repair, or question the bond.
Late progression turns bearer and artifact into a recognized lineage node whose actions can influence nations, faiths, and relic politics.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The artifact remembers older wielders, older wars, and older claims, so bonding with it means inheriting history rather than starting clean.
Observers may treat the bearer as a mouthpiece, usurper, chosen heir, or temporary caretaker depending on the relic's reputation.
Every deepening of the bond raises the question of whether the wielder is shaping the artifact or being shaped by it.
questHooks: Complete an awakening trial that reveals whether the artifact truly chose you or is only tolerating your use temporarily.
Recover missing relic-memory fragments before a rival claimant can use them to challenge your legitimacy.
Decide whether to restore a damaged artifact law that would make you stronger but bind you to an older oath you do not agree with.

name: Dragon Obedience Aura
summary: A draconic hierarchy Authority that compels dragons and related apex beings to recognize precedence, caution, or conditional obedience.
description: Dragon Obedience Aura is an Authority that compels high-order draconic beings to recognize hierarchy, caution, or negotiated submission. It belongs in the Authority category because it is a command right over a storied power class rather than a broad all-purpose System. The bearer does not automatically own all dragons, but radiates a law of precedence that can force hesitation, challenge-response ritual, or conditional obedience in beings that ordinarily answer to no one. Its progression bias favors social intimidation, monster control, and strategic dominance over rare apex encounters rather than universal usefulness in mundane fights. The main tradeoff is backlash, because dragons are proud, ancient, and politically entangled creatures whose coerced obedience generates grudges, tests, and retaliatory plots. In the world, Dragon Obedience Aura is legendary because even partial control over dragon behavior alters war, trade, religion, and ecology. It also remains morally unstable, since there is a meaningful difference between rightful command, temporary restraint, and abusive enslavement. It remains lore-safe because the Authority works on a specific exalted class of beings with their own resistance tiers, ancient laws, and superior exceptions rather than acting as a generic domination power.
coreLoop: Project draconic precedence to force hesitation, submission checks, or ritual acknowledgment from dragons and related apex beings.
Use challenge, negotiation, or disciplined dominance to convert that opening into pacts, restraint, or conditional obedience.
Manage the political and emotional aftermath because every dragon commanded today is a memory-bearing power tomorrow.
Trigger Dragon Obedience Aura's authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression affects lesser drakes, dragonkin, and weakened apex creatures through intimidation and ritual challenge states.
Mid progression extends pressure to true dragons, mount eligibility, and battlefield suppression windows against draconic threats.
Late progression turns the Aura into a diplomatic and military crisis tool because elder dragons must at least acknowledge the bearer's presence.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every successful command creates memory, and dragons are the kind of beings who remember slights for centuries.
The Authority constantly blurs the line between rightful dominance, negotiated respect, and deeply dangerous humiliation.
Dragon clans, hatcheries, and beast lords all react differently depending on whether the bearer commands with restraint or predation.
questHooks: Calm a rampaging dragon without killing it and decide whether saving the region is worth creating a lifelong draconic enemy.
Enter a hatchery court where every word is a challenge-response ritual and one false command could start a war.
Face an elder wyrm who agrees to obey only if you first prove that your Authority is something more than humiliation dressed as law.

name: Critical Strike Mandate
summary: A precision Authority that declares certain blows decisive and bends probability toward lethal certainty within strict conditions.
description: Critical Strike Mandate is an Authority that governs the law of decisive impact rather than damage in general. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command over a narrow combat truth: under the right conditions, the bearer may declare that a strike lands as a telling, law-backed critical event. The Authority does not mean every attack becomes unfair, but that the bearer can accumulate certainty and then spend it to force decisive moments past ordinary probability. Its progression bias favors setup, accuracy, timing, and ruthless finish windows rather than endless sustained output. The bearer becomes most frightening against targets who rely on armor, durability, or a belief that attrition will always outlast burst precision. The main tradeoff is narrowness, because a mandate over decisive hits is strongest when the bearer can create clean openings and much weaker against chaos, denial, or dispersed battlefields. In the world, Critical Strike Mandate should feel like a duelist's horror and an executioner's miracle because it makes rare killing moments feel chosen rather than lucky. It remains lore-safe because certainty must be charged, declared, and earned inside combat conditions, and because no precision law exceeds Void, Grandmother Void, or perfect invulnerability enforced by stronger powers.
coreLoop: Land hits to charge the 'Certainty' meter.
Expend Certainty to guarantee a critical strike.
Chain criticals to enter a 'Shatter' state, boosting critical damage.
Trigger Critical Strike Mandate's authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth improves certainty generation, exposes weak-point conditions more clearly, and lets the bearer prepare one reliable decisive window per encounter.
Mid progression unlocks chained precision states, law-backed shatter effects, and conditional finishers that punish overconfident tanks or duelists.
Late progression turns the bearer into a feared execution specialist who can define one strike as the battle's true point of no return.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Enemies with high defense become trivial, shifting the balance of power.
Beings of fate and luck see you as an anomaly that must be corrected.
Factions notice Critical Strike Mandate and shift diplomacy based on your growth curve and threat profile.
questHooks: Shatter a legendary, 'unbreakable' artifact.
Win a duel where you are only allowed to deal damage via critical hits.
Complete a category-specific trial to unlock the next Critical Strike Mandate milestone.

name: Demonic Heritage Throne
summary: An infernal Authority that crowns a bloodline claimant with command over demons, sin-charged law, and hellish rank.
description: Demonic Heritage Throne is an Authority that awakens a ruling infernal bloodline and seats the bearer in a contested hellish hierarchy. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command over lesser demons, sin-aligned edicts, and infernal precedence within a specific heritage or throne line. The bearer becomes more than a corrupt spellcaster; they become a claimant whose words can bind, tempt, elevate, or punish beings recognized by demonic law. Its progression bias favors rank ascent, domain sin refinement, and ruthless command rather than broad neutral utility. The Authority grows strongest where corruption, contracts, or hell-linked territory reinforce the throne's legitimacy. The main tradeoff is contamination, because infernal rule feeds on temptation, cruelty, compromise, and the gradual erosion of clean human motive. In the world, Demonic Heritage Throne should trigger fear, cult devotion, and immediate holy response because people understand that a throne claimant can turn local suffering into a power base. It remains lore-safe because even a demonic throne is still bound to lineage, contract, rank, and contested dominion, and because every infernal crown remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Embrace demonic temptations to unlock 'Infernal Seals'.
Use 'Demonic Edicts' to command, bind, or banish supernatural entities.
Consume mortal sins or chaos to fuel your demonic abilities.
Trigger Demonic Heritage Throne's authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth secures a recognized infernal claim, minor command over lesser demons, and a first sin-domain that shapes the throne's voice.
Mid progression expands into contract enforcement, greater-rank command disputes, and local hell-zone influence that can stain territory or institutions.
Late progression seats the bearer as a terrifying court power whose infernal decrees reshape whole factions through fear, vice, and obligation.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Angelic or holy orders actively hunt you down.
Demons both challenge your authority and try to curry your favor.
Factions notice Demonic Heritage Throne and shift diplomacy based on your growth curve and threat profile.
questHooks: Usurp the throne of a rival demon lord.
Corrupt a sacred site to establish a permanent gateway to your domain.
Complete a category-specific trial to unlock the next Demonic Heritage Throne milestone.

name: Damage Reflection Field
summary: A retributive Authority that turns incoming harm into lawful backlash within a bounded field of punishment.
description: Damage Reflection Field is an Authority that governs retaliatory return rather than simple defense. It belongs in the Authority category because it gives the bearer command over a bounded law of retribution inside a defined defensive field. Harm that enters this field can be judged, mirrored, intensified, or transmuted back toward its source according to the Authority's rules. Its progression bias favors endurance, timing, and punishment of overcommitment rather than pure mitigation or passive tanking. The bearer becomes strongest against enemies who rely on burst damage, arrogance, or mindless repetition of force. The main tradeoff is exposure, because reflection requires enduring real pressure and can be overwhelmed by dispersion, denial, or attacks that never fully enter the field's judgment. In the world, Damage Reflection Field should feel unnerving because it makes violence morally and mechanically unsafe for those who deliver it carelessly. It remains lore-safe because the field only governs harm within its jurisdiction, can be counterplayed, and stays beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and stronger laws of immunity and negation.
coreLoop: Establish the field of retribution and bait enemies into committing meaningful force inside its lawful boundary.
Convert judged incoming damage into reflected punishment, retrition charge, or empowered counter-effects based on how recklessly the enemy attacked.
Release stored retribution at the right moment before the field collapses under pressure, denial, or misread threat profiles.
Trigger Damage Reflection Field's authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth improves reflection efficiency, field clarity, and the bearer's ability to convert straightforward attacks into safe retaliation.
Mid progression unlocks rider effects such as stun, shred, burnback, or judgment marks on attackers who keep violating the field.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying punitive fortress whose enemies can destroy themselves simply by refusing to respect its law.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Assassins and burst specialists begin to treat you as a walking nightmare because their best weapons become evidence against them.
Allies may mistake your punishment field for invulnerability until they see what it costs to hold the line for too long.
The Authority constantly asks whether retribution is justice, deterrence, or simply another hunger for violence dressed in cleaner language.
questHooks: Defeat a duel champion using only reflected punishment after they publicly swore no defense could ever stop their style.
Hold a gate by forcing a superior enemy force to break itself against your field long enough for evacuation to finish.
Learn whether a legendary mirror relic amplifies your Authority or secretly judges you by the same pain you return to others.

name: Law Comprehension Codex
summary: A jurisprudential Authority that traces local laws, interprets their clauses, and imposes bounded rule edits within understood domains.
description: Law Comprehension Codex is an Authority that grants the bearer ruling-grade understanding of how specific laws in the world are structured and enforced. It belongs in the Authority category because it governs command through interpreted law, lawful override windows, and domain-limited rule precedence rather than through generic intelligence or reality editing. The bearer learns to trace a phenomenon, identify the governing clause behind it, and then exploit or temporarily amend that clause where they have earned standing. Its progression bias favors study, precision, and local dominion over a known rule set rather than reckless omnidirectional power. The Authority is strongest when the bearer has properly read a site, artifact, ritual, or enemy technique before trying to intervene. The main tradeoff is interpretive burden, because misunderstanding the active law can lead to failed commands, catastrophic backlash, or accidental empowerment of the very rule being challenged. In the world, Law Comprehension Codex should terrify scholars, judges, mages, and primordial guardians because it turns knowledge into a form of jurisdiction. It remains lore-safe because the Codex only governs laws that can be traced, understood, and locally contested, and because no interpreted clause can outrank Void, Grandmother Void, or the highest cosmic order.
coreLoop: Trace a natural, magical, or social phenomenon until the Codex identifies the governing law fragment behind it.
Accumulate lawful standing and fragments so the bearer can issue a bounded amendment, suspension, or counter-clause inside that domain.
Exploit the edited law before correction pressure, hostile guardians, or missing context collapse the advantage.
Trigger Law Comprehension Codex's authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth improves law tracing, fragment storage, and safe intervention in narrow local rules such as motion, heat, or ritual sequencing.
Mid progression unlocks codified domains, chained clause edits, and stronger standing against magical, contractual, or battlefield laws.
Late progression turns the bearer into a feared juris-architect who can make even mighty powers obey the letter of a law they failed to read closely enough.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Reality does not merely warp around you; it starts revealing which clauses people have trusted without ever understanding.
Judges, archivists, and primordial custodians all have reasons to either recruit you or bury the Codex before it destabilizes their order.
The deeper your understanding grows, the harder it becomes to pretend the world was ever held together by simple rules.
questHooks: Repair a corrupted region by identifying which foundational law was broken and who benefits from keeping it unstable.
Win a battle against a stronger foe by forcing their signature technique to obey an older clause it normally ignores.
Steal a sealed page of the Codex from a guardian court that insists mortals must never learn how law is actually written.

name: Divine Champion (God's Chosen)
summary: A consecrated Authority that appoints the bearer as a god-backed champion with domain-limited miracles, command, and holy legitimacy.
description: Divine Champion is an Authority that marks the bearer as a chosen combat and judgment instrument of a deity or pantheon. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through sanctioned holy office, domain-backed miracles, and the right to act in a god's name within bounded sacred scope. The bearer does not simply receive blessings, but becomes a recognized champion whose title carries real metaphysical weight with allies, enemies, relics, and rites. Its progression bias favors devotion, trial completion, public legitimacy, and faithful action rather than private self-optimization. The Authority grows strongest when the champion acts within the moral, ritual, or jurisdictional lane of their patron's sphere. The main tradeoff is burden, because divine office comes with vows, scrutiny, and the constant risk of misrepresenting a higher will. In the world, Divine Champion should command reverence, envy, and political alarm because a god-backed mortal can overturn earthly balances without being a god themselves. It remains lore-safe because the champion's power is office-bound, patron-limited, and revocable, and because even divine appointment remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Act under the champion's seal to invoke miracles, rally allies, and enforce the patron's sacred right within situations the office recognizes.
Complete divine trials, uphold vows, and resolve patron-aligned crises to deepen legitimacy and widen the office's lawful reach.
Manage public worship, rival clergy, and the cost of being the mortal face of a power far larger than yourself.
Trigger Divine Champion (God's Chosen)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants the champion's seal, minor miracles, and recognized authority in the patron's first sphere such as war, judgment, healing, or flame.
Mid progression expands into relic command, group blessing fields, and stronger miracle law when the champion acts under rite or sanction.
Late progression turns the bearer into a world-shaping sacred officer whose arrival can sanctify battlefields, rally nations, or condemn blasphemous powers.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Priests and rulers alike must decide whether you are a savior, a political threat, or the most expensive ally they have ever seen.
Your victories are never fully private because every miracle becomes evidence for or against the patron you represent.
The more clearly you hear divine purpose, the harder it becomes to separate your own desires from the office speaking through you.
questHooks: Prove your office in a public trial where rival faiths are waiting for one failed miracle to discredit the god behind you.
Recover a relic that will either strengthen your patron's authority in the world or expose why your appointment was contested from the start.
Choose whether to obey a divine command that would save a kingdom at the cost of betraying someone innocent.

name: Heaven's Mandate (Fate's Favorite)
summary: A fate-crowned Authority that marks the bearer as heaven-backed within a narrow but terrifying regime of legitimacy, fortune, and succession.
description: Heaven's Mandate is an Authority that marks the bearer as a recognized favorite of fate, order, or heavenly legitimacy. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through sanctioned precedence, karmic endorsement, and the right to occupy a role that the world itself has partially acknowledged. The bearer does not simply get lucky, but benefits from a regime of legitimacy that nudges events, loyalty, and opportunity toward their continued rise. Its progression bias favors rulership, public prominence, karmic accumulation, and the ability to keep acting like someone heaven still endorses. The Authority is strongest when the bearer stands at the center of succession, governance, or civilizational turning points where legitimacy matters as much as force. The main tradeoff is visibility, because heaven-backed figures attract rebellion, envy, prophecy, and every rival who wants to prove fate has chosen incorrectly. In the world, Heaven's Mandate should feel imperial and destabilizing because once one claimant is marked, everyone else must decide whether to submit, resist, or steal the omen. It remains lore-safe because the Mandate only governs legitimacy, fortune, and role reinforcement inside bounded worldly structures, and because even heaven's favorite remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Accumulate karmic legitimacy through victories, rulership acts, omens, and public confirmations that reinforce heaven's apparent endorsement.
Spend that legitimacy to survive crises, sway succession struggles, or make key opportunities align in your favor when your claim is under pressure.
Preserve the Mandate by acting in ways that keep heaven's endorsement believable to the world and to the deeper order behind it.
Trigger Heaven's Mandate (Fate's Favorite)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth manifests as improbable survival, auspicious timing, and subtle legitimacy pressure that makes others hesitate before opposing the bearer openly.
Mid progression expands into stronger karmic favor, role reinforcement, and domain effects over court, army, or sect once the bearer is publicly established.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying claimant whose rise seems cosmically ratified until someone can prove heaven has withdrawn its hand.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every lucky turn in your favor becomes politically meaningful once people decide heaven is making statements through your life.
Rebels, prophets, and rival heirs all gain reasons to expose your failures as evidence that the Mandate was never truly yours.
The more destiny bends toward you, the more dangerous it becomes to confuse endorsement with virtue.
questHooks: Hold a collapsing realm together long enough to prove heaven has not withdrawn its favor from your rule.
Confront a rival claimant whose omens are stronger than yours but whose heart may be far less fit to rule.
Recover a lost regalia that can either confirm your legitimacy or expose that the Mandate has been contested all along.

name: Celestial Pact (Divine Contract System)
summary: A contract-bound Authority that lets the bearer exercise a patron's celestial jurisdiction through vows, service, and negotiated divine law.
description: Celestial Pact is an Authority that binds the bearer to a higher celestial being through a formal contract of service and delegated jurisdiction. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through patron-backed clauses, divine obligations, and lawful access to a specific heavenly domain rather than through generic blessing alone. The bearer becomes a mortal instrument who can invoke their patron's sanctioned powers within the scope of the pact. Its progression bias favors obedience, negotiated favor, visible service, and the careful management of duties rather than free personal ambition. The Authority is strongest when the bearer honors contract terms, fulfills patron errands, and acts within the pact's recognized sphere. The main tradeoff is dependency, because power is mediated by relationship, behavior, and the patron's willingness to continue investing authority into the mortal vessel. In the world, Celestial Pact should feel both sacred and unsettling because it makes a person into a living embassy for a higher being. It remains lore-safe because the pact delegates bounded authority, remains contestable or revocable, and keeps the bearer beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Receive authority through a living contract that specifies the patron's domain, the bearer's obligations, and the lawful shape of granted miracles.
Fulfill pact duties, complete patron missions, and cultivate renown or worship so the contract deepens rather than stagnates.
Invoke the pact's granted jurisdiction in moments where the patron's authority is recognized and the bearer is willing to pay the relational price.
Trigger Celestial Pact (Divine Contract System)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants a binding contract, first-tier boons, and a clear set of duties that define what the pact will and will not support.
Mid progression expands into stronger delegated judgments, patron channels, and the ability to negotiate amendments or deepen clauses in the relationship.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying pact envoy whose presence can bring a slice of a higher being's order into mortal affairs.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every visible miracle reminds everyone nearby that your patron has interests in this world and has chosen you as an instrument for them.
The more authority you wield, the more you must ask whether the pact is a partnership, a leash, or something more intimate and dangerous than either.
Other churches, pacts, and celestial intermediaries all have opinions about who should be allowed to negotiate with heaven directly.
questHooks: Renegotiate a pact clause before your patron's latest demand destroys the last part of your life that still feels human.
Outmaneuver a rival envoy whose contract covers the same domain but interprets divine duty in the opposite way.
Recover a lost covenant tablet that proves your patron once promised more mercy than their current clergy are willing to allow.

name: Dark Covenant (Accursed Blessing)
summary: A bargain-bound Authority that grants forbidden blessings through an active relationship with dark, predatory, or accursed powers.
description: Dark Covenant is an Authority founded on sanctioned exchange with ominous, forbidden, or predatory powers. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants a recognized right to invoke and enforce dark terms within a bounded relationship rather than building an entire independent progression engine. The bearer receives blessings, force multipliers, or law-bending clauses, but only through a living contract with appetite, debt, and metaphysical enforcement. Its progression bias favors decisive bargains, short-term leverage, and morally dangerous efficiency rather than clean sustainable advancement. The main tradeoff is obligation, because every gift implies counter-demand, and the covenant grows more intimate and expensive as the bearer leans on it. In the world, Dark Covenant is feared because it creates results too useful to ignore and costs too terrible to normalize. It is also politically ambiguous, since some cultures see it as blasphemy while others treat it as an old and respectable technology of survival. It remains lore-safe because the covenant always binds both parties inside terms, and because even powerful accursed patrons operate below the Void ceiling and can be resisted, out-negotiated, or starved.
coreLoop: Invoke contract clauses that trade permission, sacrifice, debt, or taboo offerings for immediate accursed power.
Manage the covenant relationship so the patron's hunger, personality, and demands remain exploitable rather than overwhelming.
Choose which bargains to accept, delay, reinterpret, or resist as the Authority grows stronger and more invasive.
Trigger Dark Covenant (Accursed Blessing)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression grants controlled blessings, curse clauses, and limited patron interventions that feel powerful but survivable.
Mid progression deepens the relationship into a true covenant with named terms, escalating debt, and patron-specific manifestations of authority.
Late progression creates terrifying leverage where one bargain can swing a war, save a city, or doom a soul depending on what the bearer agrees to pay.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Authority always forces the question of whether survival purchased through darkness is wisdom, weakness, or the beginning of surrender.
Patrons are never neutral sources of power, which means every miracle risks becoming a negotiation scene disguised as combat utility.
Observers may fear the bearer less for what they can do now than for what they might be asked to become later.
questHooks: Renegotiate a covenant clause before the promised price comes due in a way that would destroy someone you were trying to protect.
Track down a prior covenant bearer whose failed bargains left loopholes, warnings, and enemies still hunting the contract line.
Choose whether to accept an emergency patron gift that can save the region now but will bind you to a darker long-term obligation.

name: Star-Scion Matrix (Constellation Bond)
summary: A starline Authority that seats the bearer beneath a specific celestial body or constellation and lets its law descend through them.
description: Star-Scion Matrix is an Authority that links the bearer's soul to a specific star, constellation, or celestial principle with ruling significance. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through starline inheritance, astral precedence, and direct descent of a bounded celestial law. The bearer becomes a scion, not merely a mage, meaning their bond carries recognized weight with omens, navigators, cults, and other sky-touched powers. Its progression bias favors celestial timing, identity alignment, and the disciplined cultivation of a star-specific office rather than broad generic spell growth. The Authority is strongest when the bearer's actions resonate with the bonded star's symbolic nature and the current sky supports that resonance. The main tradeoff is cyclic vulnerability, because eclipses, adverse alignments, daylight conditions, or starline corruption can sharply alter performance. In the world, Star-Scion Matrix should feel aristocratic and cosmic at once because it makes the bearer a living extension of a star's will or meaning. It remains lore-safe because the Authority governs a bounded celestial lineage and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest law of the heavens.
coreLoop: Cultivate resonance with the bonded star or constellation until its law can descend through the scion in stable, named expressions.
Use celestial events, night conditions, and symbolic acts aligned with the starline to deepen command and unlock stronger manifestations.
Protect the star bond from eclipse, corruption, rival scions, and misalignment that would turn inherited law against the bearer.
Trigger Star-Scion Matrix (Constellation Bond)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants an identifiable starline bond, a first descended aspect, and practical influence over travel, combat, or fate in the star's lane.
Mid progression expands into stronger aspect descent, star-path travel, and more explicit authority over those who recognize the same celestial order.
Late progression turns the bearer into a radiant scion whose presence can make whole factions read the sky differently around them.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every celestial event becomes personal once your life is visibly chained to the mood and motion of one starline.
Rival scions, astrologers, and omencasters may see you as heir, usurper, or catastrophic omen depending on what your star means to them.
The more deeply the Matrix descends, the harder it becomes to tell where your ambitions end and your star's pattern begins.
questHooks: Reignite a dimming starline before your authority collapses and your enemies claim the sky has abandoned you.
Contest a rival scion during a rare conjunction that will decide whose interpretation of the same constellation becomes dominant.
Retrieve a fallen fragment of your bonded star from a crater cult that believes no mortal should carry that much sky inside them.

name: Summoned Hero (System-Mandated Savior)
summary: A world-sanctioned Authority that appoints the bearer as a recognized hero and grants narrow but terrifying savior-grade legitimacy.
description: Summoned Hero is an Authority that installs the bearer into a world-recognized role of sanctioned salvation. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through title, mandate, and role legitimacy rather than through a free-floating System of personal growth alone. The bearer is not simply powerful; they become the authorized hero for a specific crisis, enemy class, or era-defining threat. Its progression bias favors heroic milestones, public victories, and fulfilling the role's sanctioned duties rather than unrestricted self-direction. The Authority becomes most potent against the threat profile it was summoned or anointed to answer, which keeps its savior-grade power from dissolving into generic supremacy. The main tradeoff is burden of role, because everyone from kings to commoners begins projecting expectation, gratitude, fear, and control onto the person carrying the title. In the world, Summoned Hero should feel both inspirational and destabilizing because once a world has named its savior, many institutions stop behaving as if ordinary politics still apply. It remains lore-safe because the hero's title governs a bounded role with specific enemies, rites, and duties, and because even a sanctioned savior remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Answer hero-mandated threats, complete role-defining quests, and prove to the world that the title's legitimacy is not misplaced.
Convert major victories into stronger hero rights such as relic access, ally-rally effects, and sharper advantages against the sanctioned enemy profile.
Balance personal will against the crushing expectations of rulers, systems, and civilians who all think the hero exists for their salvation first.
Trigger Summoned Hero (System-Mandated Savior)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants the hero title, access to role-locked relics or skills, and strong leverage against the first crisis the summoning was meant to solve.
Mid progression expands into broader hero rights, visible aura effects, and milestone unlocks tied to defeating designated calamities or lords.
Late progression turns the bearer into a living symbol whose title can rally armies, terrify villain factions, and reshape whole wars around their presence.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The title turns every victory into public myth and every failure into a political emergency that no one will let stay private.
People saved by the hero may worship, resent, or try to own the person behind the role once their survival starts depending on it.
The deeper you grow into the title, the more dangerous it becomes to ask whether the world wanted a savior or only a weapon.
questHooks: Choose whether to keep obeying the summons after learning the world lied about who the true enemy was.
Recover a role-locked relic before a rival claimant proves the hero title can be transferred or stolen.
Defeat the designated calamity only to discover that fulfilling the role may erase the part of you that ever wanted to go home.

name: Territory Lord Interface (Base-Building Sovereign)
summary: A governance Authority that lets the bearer issue lordly commands through a territory-management interface tied to lawful domain growth.
description: Territory Lord Interface is an Authority that converts rulership and land stewardship into a direct command layer the bearer can access. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants jurisdiction over buildings, projects, labor assignment, and local edicts inside a recognized territory. The bearer does not merely manage a city more efficiently, but gains the lawful right to impose structured development priorities that reshape local productivity and defense. Its progression bias favors planning, logistics, and institutional growth rather than free-roaming heroics. The Authority is strongest where the bearer truly holds recognized land, resources, and subjects willing or forced to live under its interface. The main tradeoff is dependence on governance, because neglected territory, bad policy, corruption, or resource starvation can turn the interface from miracle into administrative disaster. In the world, Territory Lord Interface should feel revolutionary because it gives one ruler simulation-grade leverage over real settlements and warfronts. It remains lore-safe because the interface only commands a bounded territory and its lawful projects, and because even its best governance remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Claim or maintain a lawful territory, then use the interface to assign projects, structures, labor priorities, and regional bonuses.
Convert territory output into stronger lordly authority, better infrastructure, and more ambitious projects that reshape local life.
Balance prosperity, defense, and legitimacy so the same tools that can build a kingdom do not instead automate collapse.
Trigger Territory Lord Interface (Base-Building Sovereign)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks basic build orders, resource-routing panels, and local buffs that make a small settlement meaningfully easier to protect and grow.
Mid progression expands into specialized districts, militia logistics, outpost links, and stronger law-of-the-land effects across the domain.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying territorial executive who can scale a frontier holding into a fortified polity at unnatural speed.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: To your people the interface looks like miraculous governance, while rivals see it as a cheating machine for statecraft.
Every improvement to the land changes what kind of ruler you are becoming, because optimization always has a human cost somewhere.
The better the territory runs, the less room there is to pretend your political decisions are merely personal preferences.
questHooks: Stabilize a starving domain before the same interface that made it prosper also makes its collapse impossibly efficient.
Break a rival lord's project chain before their engineered border towns become an unassailable machine state.
Choose whether to spend your next major build phase on walls, hospitals, shrines, or extraction knowing one neglected need will erupt later.

name: Domain Sovereign (Personal Domain Expansion)
summary: A bounded-field Authority that lets the bearer impose a personal domain whose laws locally outrank ordinary combat assumptions.
description: Domain Sovereign is an Authority that allows the bearer to project a bounded personal domain governed by their own declared law. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command over a specific field of space where the bearer's rule has precedence, rather than granting unrestricted control over reality at large. Inside that domain, conditions can be modified to reflect the sovereign's principle, such as priority of motion, heat tolerance, sensory distortion, or suppression of enemy technique lanes. Its progression bias favors territorial timing, decisive activation, and the sharpening of one governing law rather than broad utility across every situation. The Authority is strongest when the bearer can force enemies to remain inside the field long enough for its rule to matter. The main tradeoff is boundedness, because the domain costs heavily to establish, can be contested by stronger fields, and loses much of its terror once opponents escape or refuse the terms. In the world, Domain Sovereign should feel awe-inspiring because it visibly announces that someone has become a local ruler of conditions. It remains lore-safe because the domain is spatially bounded, law-limited, and still subordinate to Void, Grandmother Void, and stronger sovereign orders.
coreLoop: Declare or unfold a bounded domain whose governing law favors the bearer and pressures enemies to fight on its terms.
Exploit the domain's altered rules before opponents can break, escape, or overwrite the field with stronger authority.
Refine the governing law over time so the domain becomes sharper, more recognizable, and more difficult to contest.
Trigger Domain Sovereign (Personal Domain Expansion)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants a small but reliable domain with one clean law that changes how a duel or skirmish must be fought.
Mid progression expands field stability, layered law effects, and the ability to carry the domain into more hostile or crowded battle spaces.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying battlefield sovereign whose activation can redefine the meaning of terrain itself for everyone nearby.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: When your domain opens, witnesses feel the world become someone else's courtroom, temple, or killing ground for a few terrible moments.
Rivals who survive it will obsess over learning exactly what law you imposed and how to deny it next time.
The more absolute your field feels, the more dangerous it becomes to believe your rule should continue once the boundary ends.
questHooks: Win a clash between rival domains where the outcome will determine whose local law becomes dominant in a sacred battleground.
Stabilize a domain principle that keeps mutating under pressure before it tears your own battlefield advantage apart.
Choose whether to teach disciples your domain law, knowing each student risks diluting or corrupting the sovereign idea behind it.

name: Nature's Avatar (World Elemental Integration)
summary: An elemental-biospheric Authority that makes the bearer a recognized voice of land, weather, and living ecological force.
description: Nature's Avatar is an Authority that binds the bearer to a major biospheric or elemental order of the world. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command over a natural domain such as forest, storm, river, growth, or beast ecology rather than broad generic spell access. The bearer becomes a recognized mouthpiece of that domain, able to summon, calm, reshape, or intensify its living processes. Its progression bias favors harmony, place-attunement, and reciprocal stewardship rather than extractive power for its own sake. The Authority is strongest where the chosen domain is vibrant, present, and not violently severed from itself by corruption or artificial suppression. The main tradeoff is reciprocity, because abusing the domain for selfish force can weaken the bond or make the natural order itself turn hostile. In the world, Nature's Avatar should feel primal, numinous, and politically dangerous because entire regions may begin to answer more readily to one person than to local rulers. It remains lore-safe because the Authority governs one ecological lane at a time, depends on living systems, and remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Attune to the chosen natural domain and act in ways that deepen mutual recognition between bearer and land, weather, beast, or element.
Command the domain through invocation, shaping, and communion once local natural systems recognize your right to speak for them.
Preserve the bond by balancing protection, use, and sacrifice so the same world-force that empowers you does not reject you.
Trigger Nature's Avatar (World Elemental Integration)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants local communion, modest environmental shaping, and a first true sign that nature recognizes your authority.
Mid progression expands into regional weather or biome influence, spirit recognition, and stronger command over creatures or elemental flows in your lane.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying ecological sovereign whose arrival can change the mood and function of whole landscapes.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Settlers, druids, and states all fear different things when the land starts listening to one person's voice.
The more deeply you merge with the domain, the harder it becomes to decide where your own desires end and the world's begin.
Every miracle of rain, bloom, flood, or wildfire leaves a political footprint because someone always benefits and someone always pays.
questHooks: Heal a wounded biome before rival powers convince the land that civilization only knows how to cut and burn.
Choose whether to unleash a devastating natural correction against invaders even though innocents will be caught inside it.
Win the right to command an ancient spirit host that will obey only someone who proves they can protect more than they consume.

name: Law Manipulator (World Rule Bender)
summary: A high-order Authority that lets the bearer impose specific world-rule distortions within tightly bounded lawful scope.
description: Law Manipulator is an Authority that grants the bearer command over a small set of fundamental world rules within limited scope. It belongs in the Authority category because it governs specific laws such as weight, heat, motion, or sequence through narrow sovereign intervention rather than open-ended reality authorship. The bearer is not omniscient about law, but gains the right to impose or distort chosen rules inside a battlefield, ritual, or prepared zone. Its progression bias favors enlightenment, clarity of principle, and disciplined restriction rather than stacking every possible cheat at once. The Authority becomes strongest when the bearer understands exactly which law must bend and where the bend will matter most. The main tradeoff is precision burden, because the wrong law, the wrong scope, or the wrong timing can waste power or catastrophically destabilize the scene. In the world, Law Manipulator should feel terrifyingly intellectual because it makes a person's understanding into a direct command over what others assumed was fixed. It remains lore-safe because the Authority operates through bounded law selection, contest, and cost, and remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Select the governing law that matters most to the current conflict or ritual instead of trying to dominate every variable at once.
Impose a bounded distortion in a defined scope where the chosen law now favors the bearer or punishes the unprepared.
Manage backlash, counter-law pressure, and the risk that the altered rule will harm allies or terrain if held too long.
Trigger Law Manipulator (World Rule Bender)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants one or two modest law distortions with strict scope, duration, and cost boundaries.
Mid progression expands into sharper distortions, better law pairing, and stronger resistance against enemies who rely on one fixed rule too heavily.
Late progression turns the bearer into a feared law duelist who wins not by overpowering reality, but by choosing exactly which rule everyone must suddenly survive.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: People stop calling you powerful and start calling you dangerous once they realize you can make certainty itself feel conditional.
Every new law you claim changes how scholars, rulers, and other authorities classify you, because some rules are more taboo to touch than others.
The more elegantly you solve problems through rule distortion, the more temptation there is to treat all resistance as merely incorrect physics.
questHooks: Steal a forbidden law-principle from an archive that executed the last person who tried to bind it.
Survive a duel against another law-bearer where victory goes to whoever defines the battlefield's governing rule first.
Decide whether to seal a dangerous law forever or keep it because too many future crises may demand its use.

name: Blood Pact Warlock (Contracted Power)
summary: A dark-contract Authority that grants the bearer borrowed command through blood-sealed obligations, patron claims, and dangerous power rights.
description: Blood Pact Warlock is an Authority that binds the bearer to a patron through blood-sealed obligation and dangerous contractual power. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through the legal and symbolic force of a blood pact, not merely by borrowing spells from something stronger. The bearer becomes an authorized vessel for a patron's dark jurisdiction, able to command pact-granted effects, entities, and sanctions within the contract's scope. Its progression bias favors negotiation, sacrifice, and increasingly severe exchanges of self or service rather than clean personal growth. The Authority is strongest when the pact is active, the debt is current, and the patron's sphere overlaps with the crisis at hand. The main tradeoff is corrosive dependency, because every stronger use deepens entanglement with a will that expects repayment. In the world, Blood Pact Warlock should feel feared and fascinating because it turns private desperation into a recognizable form of dark office. It remains lore-safe because the authority is contract-bound, contestable, and purchased at escalating cost, and because even blood law remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Invoke the blood pact to access domain-specific commands, power rights, and patron-backed manifestations that ordinary casters cannot sustain.
Renegotiate or deepen the pact through sacrifice, service, or risk when greater authority is needed than the current contract permits.
Manage debt, corruption, and patron pressure so each use does not quietly transfer more of your life than you intended to spend.
Trigger Blood Pact Warlock (Contracted Power)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants a dangerous but usable pact mark, first-tier authority effects, and a clear debt structure the bearer must survive.
Mid progression expands into stronger patron manifestations, enforcement clauses, and partial command over beings or spaces touched by the same blood law.
Late progression turns the bearer into a feared contract sovereign whose words can bind, punish, or unleash horrors at the cost of becoming harder to call wholly mortal.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every pact mark on your body is a sentence in a contract others can learn to fear, read, or exploit.
People near you must guess whether they are dealing with a desperate mortal using dark office or a person already halfway replaced by the patron's claim.
The more elegant your command becomes, the more frightening it is that power now speaks in a language written with your own blood.
questHooks: Break or rewrite one clause of the pact before your patron cashes it in during the worst possible crisis.
Hunt a rival warlock whose contract exposes a weakness in your own authority's legal foundation.
Choose whether to buy enough power to save a city tonight even though tomorrow's debt may ruin everything you value.

name: Divinity Pathway
summary: Structured ascension with rites, domains, worship, and the burdens of approaching godhood.
description: Divinity Pathway is a Path that raises a mortal toward godhood through rites, domains, worship, and ascending sacred legitimacy. It belongs in the Path category because it is a structured route of apotheosis, not a ready-made divine Authority granted in full at the start. The bearer chooses or discovers a domain and then builds themselves into its proper vessel through deeds, followers, rites, and trials of worthiness. Its progression bias favors symbolic action, public consequence, and alignment between identity and portfolio rather than private isolated growth. The main tradeoff is burden, because every step toward divinity increases responsibility, scrutiny, and the danger of becoming trapped by the domain one is trying to embody. In the world, Divinity Pathway is explosive because rising gods challenge pantheons, priesthoods, and entire metaphysical balances of prayer and power. It is also psychologically transformative, since the bearer slowly stops living as a single person and starts living as a locus of expectation, doctrine, and sacred function. It remains lore-safe because the Path builds divinity through recognition, sacrifice, and domain coherence beneath the higher cosmic order rather than letting a mortal simply declare themselves supreme.
coreLoop: Choose, inherit, or discover a divine portfolio and begin acting in ways that make the bearer a believable vessel for that sacred function.
Gather followers, rites, symbols, and domain-aligned deeds that convert public recognition into sacred legitimacy.
Cross ascending trials where worthiness, sacrifice, and domain coherence must survive pressure before the next divine tier becomes stable.
Trigger Divinity Pathway's path protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression grants minor blessings, rites, and portfolio-linked signs that suggest divinity is possible but unproven.
Mid progression turns the bearer into an active sacred node whose domain begins altering followers, places, and expectations around them.
Late progression approaches true godhood, where avatars, regional sacred law, and domain burdens reshape both personal life and world order.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Path makes worship materially relevant, which means belief, doubt, reform, and heresy all become direct threats or resources.
Every rise in divine status changes the bearer's personality pressure because domains want to be embodied, not merely carried.
Pantheons, prophets, and philosophers all react strongly when a new god-path opens in a world that thought its sacred order was settled.
questHooks: Decide whether to accept a flood of desperate worship that strengthens your Path but binds you to a domain role you are not ready to inhabit.
Recover a lost relic of your portfolio before an older god uses it to prove your ascension is illegitimate.
Stop a rival faith from poisoning your domain with a doctrine that would make your next divine tier impossible to stabilize.

name: Monster Evolution Path (Beast Progression)
summary: A transformation Path that advances through staged species evolution instead of ordinary class or level identity alone.
description: Monster Evolution Path is a Path that turns the bearer's growth into staged species transformation rather than ordinary class advancement. It belongs in the Path category because its core promise is long-form metamorphosis, not one overwhelming cheat or one narrow command right. The bearer accumulates energy, traits, and qualifying conditions until they reach an evolution threshold and become a stronger lifeform with new instincts, abilities, and physical law. Its progression bias favors survival, adaptation, predation, and repeated thresholds of irreversible becoming rather than stable civilized optimization. The main tradeoff is alienation, because every successful evolution makes the bearer stronger while also increasing the social, biological, and psychological distance between their new form and their old identity. In the world, Monster Evolution Path is feared, exoticized, or hunted because it collapses the monster and hero ladders into one personal ascent. It also produces visible consequence, since each stage affects mobility, appetite, vulnerabilities, social access, and how different factions classify the bearer. It remains lore-safe because every ascent is still earned through energy, survival, and compatible evolution criteria, and because not all branches are stable, respected, or reversible.
coreLoop: Accumulate evolution energy, traits, biomass, or qualifying conditions through survival, predation, adaptation, and environmental pressure.
Reach a threshold where the current body can no longer contain its own growth and must transform into a stronger species state.
Learn to live with the new form's instincts, capabilities, and vulnerabilities before pursuing the next irreversible stage.
Trigger Monster Evolution Path (Beast Progression)'s path protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression reveals that growth is species-gated, with low forms evolving into sharper predator or survival variants under real pressure.
Mid progression unlocks branch choices where evolution starts shaping role, instincts, and social readability as much as combat power.
Late progression creates apex or mythic forms whose bodies obey different physical assumptions than their original mortal stage.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every evolution changes not just strength, but classification, making allies and enemies reconsider whether the bearer still belongs where they began.
Visible transformation invites fascination, fear, hunting, and exploitation from anyone who thinks monster growth should be caged or weaponized.
The Path creates constant identity tension because surviving the next stage may require embracing instincts that were once unthinkable.
questHooks: Secure an evolution ground before hostile hunters or rival monsters force your next threshold under the worst possible conditions.
Choose between two incompatible species branches knowing one preserves social access while the other offers the power needed to survive.
Track down the remains of a failed apex evolution to learn which instincts consume bearers who climb too fast.

name: Cultivation Ascension Path (Realm Breaker)
summary: A realm-based refinement Path that advances through internal breakthroughs, tribulations, and disciplined ascension.
description: Cultivation Ascension Path is a Path that advances the bearer through discrete realms of internal refinement, breakthrough, and spiritual authority. It belongs in the Path category because it reshapes the bearer through long discipline, bottlenecks, and metaphysical transformation rather than handing out instant supremacy. The bearer climbs through stages of energy gathering, refinement, consolidation, and transcendence, each of which changes what their body, soul, and will can support. Its progression bias favors discipline, isolation, preparation, and breakthrough timing over ordinary level-based convenience. The main tradeoff is bottleneck pressure, because higher realms demand rare resources, life-risking tribulations, and a level of self-mastery that raw talent alone cannot solve. In the world, Cultivation Ascension Path feels old, respected, and destabilizing, especially in settings where most people follow simpler class or level structures. It also creates an outsider effect in mixed systems, since a cultivator is often operating according to a different logic than local institutions can easily regulate. It remains lore-safe because every realm still demands internal refinement, external pressure, and survival of real tests rather than arbitrary ladder-climbing.
coreLoop: Gather, circulate, and refine spiritual energy through disciplined practice instead of relying only on ordinary level progression.
Prepare for bottlenecks where body, soul, and will must all survive a breakthrough rather than merely collect enough points.
Cross each realm boundary through tribulation, internal stabilization, and a lasting change in what the bearer fundamentally is.
Trigger Cultivation Ascension Path (Realm Breaker)'s path protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression focuses on energy sense, circulation, foundation-building, and the painful correction of flawed habits.
Mid progression introduces real bottlenecks where tribulations, manuals, resources, and inner stability matter more than blind training volume.
Late progression creates realm shifts so dramatic that the bearer's lifespan, presence, and relationship to the world begin to change qualitatively.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Path makes patience and discipline narratively visible, because every breakthrough is the result of preparation rather than one dramatic lucky drop.
Mixed-system societies often treat cultivators as disruptive anomalies because their realm logic ignores local expectations about balanced advancement.
Every failed breakthrough leaves scars, debts, or cautionary stories, which makes ascension culture feel old and hard-earned.
questHooks: Find a safe breakthrough ground before your next realm tribulation arrives in the middle of a hostile campaign.
Choose whether to delay ascension for stability or force a breakthrough now because the world may not survive your caution.
Recover a forbidden manual fragment that can solve your bottleneck at the cost of changing what kind of cultivator you become.

name: Corruption Empowerment (Dark Alignment Path)
summary: A descent Path that trades stain, compromise, and identity erosion for escalating unlawful strength.
description: Corruption Empowerment is a Path that turns moral compromise, dark exposure, and identity erosion into escalating personal power. It belongs in the Path category because it is not one momentary evil buff, but a cumulative route of becoming shaped by repeated descent. The bearer gains strength through corruption thresholds that unlock darker forms, harsher instincts, and increasingly unlawful capacities. Its progression bias favors short-term advantage, ruthless efficiency, and willingness to use stained tools that others reject. The main tradeoff is degradation, because each gain risks warping judgment, severing trust, and making the bearer less capable of turning back once they have gone too far. In the world, Corruption Empowerment is treated as both temptation and warning, especially by institutions that know how many useful protectors slowly became monsters through justified exceptions. It also generates fear-based social advantages, because the visibly corrupted are often stronger than expected even when they are already collapsing internally. It remains lore-safe because corruption power still follows an exchange logic of stain for strength, and because higher tiers draw purifiers, exorcists, rival abominations, and the consequences of what was traded away.
coreLoop: Accumulate stain through dark acts, corrupted environments, forbidden power use, or deliberate acceptance of tainted shortcuts.
Cross corruption thresholds that unlock new forms, instincts, resistances, and capacities unavailable to cleaner paths.
Decide whether each descent is worth the strength gained, knowing every stage changes what kind of person the bearer is becoming.
Trigger Corruption Empowerment (Dark Alignment Path)'s path protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression grants unsettling efficiency boosts and minor unlawful abilities that make compromise look dangerously rational.
Mid progression unlocks visible corruption states, fear pressure, and dark form branches that trade humanity for escalating leverage.
Late progression creates monstrous or abyssal identities where power is immense but returning to an ordinary moral life may no longer be realistic.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Path always asks how many justified exceptions it takes before the bearer becomes the thing they feared.
Visible corruption changes how every ally, priest, and rival reads the bearer long before they know the full story.
The most dangerous moments are often the ones where descent feels reasonable rather than obviously monstrous.
questHooks: Choose whether to accept one more corruptive threshold because the clean solution will arrive too late to save the people in front of you.
Find a way to contain a new mutation before allies decide mercy means killing you before the next descent.
Track a fallen predecessor to learn which compromises gave them strength and which ones made return impossible.

name: Purity's Blessing (Light Alignment Path)
summary: A sanctifying Path that converts virtue, self-restraint, and righteous action into ascending states of holy transformation.
description: Purity's Blessing is a Path that grants power through purity, virtue, and righteousness across repeated tests of conduct and self-restraint. It belongs in the Path category because it is not one static holy blessing, but a route of becoming shaped by chosen integrity over time. The bearer advances by acts of kindness, courage, mercy, discipline, and principled refusal, gradually transforming into someone more capable of channeling holy force without breaking. Its progression bias favors moral consistency, protective action, and resistance to corruption rather than raw selfish efficiency. The main tradeoff is burden, because maintaining purity in a brutal world often demands sacrifice, lost opportunities, and the refusal of shortcuts that would make other paths easier. In the world, Purity's Blessing is inspiring but uncomfortable, because people admire holiness right up until it starts judging how they live. It also creates friction with pragmatic allies who may want results without the cost of remaining clean. It remains lore-safe because sanctification still requires behavior, endurance, and trials beneath the higher cosmic order rather than granting unconditional supremacy for simply being called good.
coreLoop: Accumulate virtue through consistent righteous action, self-restraint, and chosen sacrifice rather than mere reputation.
Cross sanctification thresholds that grant stronger holy traits, purifying effects, and deeper alignment with light-based force.
Protect that purity under pressure, because temptation, compromise, and despair can slow or stain the next stage of the Path.
Trigger Purity's Blessing (Light Alignment Path)'s path protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression grants visible grace, resistance to stain, and supportive miracles that reward clean intent and disciplined behavior.
Mid progression unlocks stronger purifying effects, anti-corruption force, and sacred form changes tied to proven worth rather than rhetoric.
Late progression approaches saintly or angelic states where the bearer's very presence alters how corruption, fear, and despair behave around them.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Path is uplifting but demanding, because every rise in holiness asks whether the bearer can remain compassionate without becoming inflexible.
People often love the idea of purity more than the reality of being judged by someone who actually lives it.
The hardest tests usually come when the most efficient solution is also the one that would stain the bearer permanently.
questHooks: Refuse a corrupt shortcut that would save lives now in order to preserve the sanctification needed for a greater future miracle.
Protect a pilgrimage route where every crisis is also a temptation test aimed at breaking your next threshold of purity.
Confront a fallen saint whose shattered Path shows exactly how righteous certainty can curdle into something cruel.

name: Fate Selection Engine
summary: A destiny-routing Framework that turns pivotal choices into binding clauses, rejected futures, and escalating fate debt.
description: Fate Selection Engine is a Framework that translates major choices into a structured lattice of allowable destiny outcomes. It belongs in the Framework category because it organizes how fate is presented, locked, and compounded rather than granting absolute authority over destiny itself. At narrative fulcrums, the bearer is offered a bounded set of Fate Clauses that each carry immediate advantage and long-tail consequences. Accepted clauses become active rails that slightly bias events, allies, and opportunities toward a chosen pattern of becoming. Rejected clauses do not vanish, but persist as Lost Fates that may later return as regret, temptation, or weaponized alternate possibility. Its progression bias favors commitment, pattern recognition, and long-range planning rather than spontaneous all-purpose dominance. The main tradeoff is fate debt, because forcing too many outcomes creates contradiction pressure, hostile prophecy, and escalating cost when reality must reconcile what was chosen against what was denied. It remains lore-safe because the Framework stays beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the deepest laws of causality, and because even strong clauses can be resisted, sabotaged, or shattered by stronger powers and terrible choices.
coreLoop: Reach a real narrative fulcrum where the Engine is willing to reveal multiple bounded Fate Clauses.
Commit to one clause to gain its immediate advantage while generating Lost Fates from the options you refused.
Exploit the chosen destiny pattern while managing the debt, prophecy pressure, and alternate-future backlash it creates.
Trigger Fate Selection Engine's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth sharpens clause clarity, reveals better consequence previews, and allows minor use of Lost Fates without immediate collapse.
Mid progression unlocks Destiny Cascades, clause chaining, and selective manipulation of enemy decision pressure around known fulcrums.
Late progression turns the bearer into a strategic nightmare who can shape campaigns by committing to one future while weaponizing the ghosts of the others.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Prophets and seers either revere you as a chosen hinge of history or condemn you as a vandal of proper destiny.
Rejected futures can return as Echoes of Regret that tempt, accuse, or briefly aid the bearer when reality thins.
Your appearance, allies, and surrounding omens gradually shift to reflect the clauses you keep choosing over and over.
questHooks: A rival fate-bearer has chosen a clause that would doom your city unless you break their pattern before it matures.
Resolve a paradox knot where two earlier commitments now demand mutually exclusive sacrifices from the same people.
Seek a buried Seed of Choice that can reveal a hidden fourth clause at the next world-shaping fulcrum.

name: Dungeon Admin Protocol
summary: A governance Framework that grants bounded administrative control over a dungeon so its rooms, spawn laws, and reward logic can be managed like infrastructure.
description: Dungeon Admin Protocol is a Framework that grants structured administrative control over a bounded dungeon environment. It belongs in the Framework category because it organizes spawn logic, room law, reward routing, and local permissions rather than acting as a top-tier personal cheat by itself. The bearer gains tools to inspect, tune, authorize, deny, or reconfigure limited aspects of a dungeon as if managing a hostile but usable growth machine. Its progression bias favors infrastructure mastery, area shaping, and long-term dungeon optimization rather than straightforward dueling strength. The main tradeoff is locality, because the Framework is strongest inside recognized dungeon spaces and only indirectly useful once the bearer steps away from their managed territory. In the world, Dungeon Admin Protocol should be treated as strategic state power because dungeons produce wealth, danger, migration, and military value at scale. It should also create political paranoia, since anyone who can alter dungeon behavior can destabilize economies, manipulate adventurer routes, or hide atrocities behind procedural walls. It remains lore-safe because administrative power is bounded by dungeon class, permissions, corruption levels, and higher forces that can revoke or contest management rights.
coreLoop: Bind to a valid dungeon node, core, or management layer that recognizes you as a lawful or stolen administrator.
Reconfigure room rules, spawn behaviors, and reward priorities to shape how the dungeon generates risk, traffic, and profit.
Defend, refine, and politically justify your administration as factions respond to the dungeon you are building.
Trigger Dungeon Admin Protocol's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks inspection tools, room permissions, and narrow spawn-routing changes inside one manageable dungeon sector.
Mid progression expands into reward-table tuning, event scripting, corruption control, and limited regional dungeon policy.
Late progression turns the bearer into a feared dungeon governor whose managed labyrinth can reshape trade, war, and migration patterns.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Dungeon-born entities may treat you as a reformer, tyrant, or false sovereign depending on how you set the rules of survival.
Rival guilds and frontier powers will quickly realize that your local management choices can decide who gets rich and who disappears.
Every administrative decree leaves a moral fingerprint, because a dungeon can be optimized for training, profit, cruelty, or all three.
questHooks: Break a corrupt guild monopoly by proving the current dungeon administration has been falsifying death and reward records.
Hold together a frontier settlement by rewriting one collapsing dungeon sector before its resource flow turns into a famine.
Decide whether to lock down a dungeon for public safety or keep it open because too many lives now depend on its output.

name: Heirline Reward Protocol
summary: A lineage Framework that converts family achievement, inheritance duty, and clan prestige into structured progression rewards.
description: Heirline Reward Protocol is a Framework that converts lineage success, inheritance obligations, and family achievement into structured progression rewards. It belongs in the Framework category because it governs how legacy milestones are recognized and distributed rather than granting direct sovereign command or a complete independent System. The bearer is plugged into a living inheritance ledger where clan victories, recovered artifacts, fulfilled vows, and preserved bloodline assets can all compound into future advantage. Its progression bias favors stewardship, dynasty-building, and intergenerational planning rather than purely solitary heroics. The main tradeoff is burden, because every gain is entangled with expectations from predecessors, descendants, and collateral relatives who believe they deserve a share of the same legacy. In the world, Heirline Reward Protocol should be politically explosive because it turns family history into measurable force and makes succession disputes mechanically meaningful. It should also create tension between merit and birth, since lineage reward can uplift a worthy heir or become a gilded prison for someone who never wanted the chain. It remains lore-safe because it organizes inherited value already present in the social and metaphysical world instead of creating aristocratic destiny from nothing.
coreLoop: Secure lineage milestones through vows kept, holdings restored, heirs protected, and family relics recovered or legitimized.
