Convert those milestones into legacy rewards, privileges, and long-horizon house advantages through the living inheritance ledger.
Manage succession politics and family expectations so the line grows stronger instead of tearing itself apart.
Trigger Heirline Reward Protocol's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks basic inheritance boons, family-vault access, and recognition of personal deeds as line-strengthening acts.
Mid progression expands into house doctrines, collateral branch management, and regional prestige that feeds future rewards.
Late progression turns the bearer into a dynastic nexus whose choices can uplift or doom generations of descendants and dependents.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Ancestors, heirs, and rival claimants all have reasons to interpret your success as part of their own inheritance story.
Every victory can trigger fresh succession conflict because the Protocol makes legacy visible enough for opportunists to quantify it.
The Framework constantly asks whether the bearer is building a home, a throne, or a prison for the people who come after them.
questHooks: Win a succession crisis without destroying the very relatives whose claims keep the house legitimate.
Recover an ancestral vault whose contents will either save your line or prove it never deserved to survive.
Choose whether a bastard branch will be brought into the legacy ledger or erased for political stability.

name: Underworld Save File
summary: A death-linked persistence Framework that carries selected memory, debt, and power fragments across terminated life segments.
description: Underworld Save File is a Framework that preserves a structured continuity record across death, descent, and return. It belongs in the Framework category because it manages persistence and transfer rules rather than directly ruling combat, knowledge, or reality on its own. The bearer gains an underworld-linked archive of state that determines what fragments of power, memory, debt, or penalty can cross from one terminated life-segment into the next. Its progression bias favors high-risk exploration and mortality negotiation because death becomes a costly checkpointing process instead of a total hard stop. The main tradeoff is contamination, since every passage through death leaves residue, attracts underworld attention, and risks carrying back more than intended. In the world, Underworld Save File should be secretive and feared because cultures rarely remain calm around proof that death has bookkeeping. It should also create legal and theological disputes about identity, ownership, and whether a returned person is continuous, copied, or indebted. It remains lore-safe because it does not abolish death, but merely formalizes what can survive it under underworld jurisdiction and at underworld cost.
coreLoop: Anchor a valid save state through underworld-recognized rites, places, debts, or contractual markers before a fatal descent or high-risk attempt.
On death or qualifying termination, preserve only the fragments the archive can legally carry back through underworld channels.
Return with retained memory, residue, and obligations while deciding whether the cost of another passage is still worth paying.
Trigger Underworld Save File's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth improves save integrity, memory carry-over, and the reliability of small retained advantages after return.
Mid progression unlocks deeper archive layers, selective fragment preservation, and bargaining leverage with underworld intermediaries.
Late progression turns the bearer into a notorious mortality negotiator whose returns carry power, debt, and scrutiny in equal measure.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every return forces the question of whether you came back whole or merely close enough to keep pretending continuity exists.
Underworld officials, grave powers, and death cults all have reasons to audit what you took across a boundary that should not be casually crossed.
Loved ones may welcome your survival while quietly wondering what else walked back through the gate with you.
questHooks: Recover a corrupted anchor before the next death writes your name into an underworld ledger you can never repay.
Prove to a hostile priesthood that your returned ally is continuous enough to keep their inheritance and vows.
Choose which fragment of a doomed life you will carry back when the archive refuses to preserve everything.

name: System Architect
summary: A meta-Framework that lets the bearer design, patch, and maintain bounded subsystems inside reality without becoming a supreme lawgiver.
description: System Architect is a Framework that allows the bearer to design, patch, or reconfigure limited structured mechanics inside reality. It belongs in the Framework category because its strength lies in organizing and rewriting subsystems rather than serving as a single overwhelming personal power fantasy. The bearer can create rulesets, interfaces, triggers, or bounded progression modules that affect items, zones, contracts, or subordinate entities. Its progression bias favors design literacy, modular thinking, and infrastructure leverage over direct raw force. The main tradeoff is complexity, because every created structure must be maintained, balanced, and defended against exploitation, corruption, or unintended emergence. In the world, System Architect should be seen as profoundly dangerous because it makes the bearer not just a user of systems but a local maker of them. It should also remain rare and controversial, since anyone who can patch reality invites fear of bugs, abuse, and private lawmaking. It remains lore-safe because architectural edits are bounded in scope, subject to stronger existing law, and vulnerable to collapse when poorly specified or opposed by higher Authorities and Systems.
coreLoop: Draft bounded rule modules, interfaces, or trigger graphs that can be safely attached to zones, items, contracts, or subordinate structures.
Deploy, monitor, and rebalance those modules as real usage reveals exploits, instability, and unintended behavior.
Harvest leverage from well-designed infrastructure while paying the ongoing maintenance cost of being your own local system engineer.
Trigger System Architect's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks small utility modules, simple triggers, and safer template-based subsystem designs.
Mid progression expands module slots, causal resilience, and the ability to compose multiple rule objects into coherent local ecosystems.
Late progression lets the bearer build feared custom infrastructures whose elegance or failure can alter whole regions and institutions.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every clever patch carries the threat that someone else will exploit it harder than you expected or harder than you can survive.
Institutions fear you because you do not simply use the world as written; you are one of the few people capable of authoring local mechanics.
The Framework naturally creates hubris stories, because elegant design and catastrophic overreach live very close together.
questHooks: Patch a failing civic defense lattice before a city discovers its trusted laws were held together by one unstable module.
Hunt a rival architect whose private subsystem has turned a border region into a self-escalating exploit.
Choose whether to publish a design that could save thousands if copied or destroy it before worse hands weaponize it.

name: Undead Legion Evolution
summary: A military Framework that treats undead forces as an evolving roster of units, doctrines, and ranked promotions.
description: Undead Legion Evolution is a Framework that manages necromantic forces as a scalable roster instead of a pile of disposable corpses. It belongs in the Framework category because it organizes recruitment, promotion, doctrine, and unit specialization rather than simply granting raw death magic by itself. The bearer gains structured control over how undead are raised, assigned, upgraded, and preserved across campaigns. Its progression bias favors logistics, force composition, and attrition management instead of lone-hero combat supremacy. The dead become more dangerous over time not only because there are more of them, but because the legion learns, stratifies, and mutates around battlefield need. The main tradeoff is maintenance pressure, because command load, supply substitutes, corruption, and morale reactions all scale with the size and sophistication of the host. In the world, Undead Legion Evolution should trigger terror, opportunism, and holy retaliation because a disciplined undead army threatens borders, labor systems, burial custom, and the legitimacy of the living. It remains lore-safe because the legion is still bounded by command capacity, corpse quality, territory, anti-undead opposition, and the spiritual consequences of fielding the dead as infrastructure.
coreLoop: Raise or recover valid dead, assign them into a structured roster, and define doctrines that shape how the legion fights.
Feed the host through battle results, corpse quality, salvage, and command investment so units can evolve beyond base forms.
Manage scale, loyalty drift, and public backlash as the army becomes more useful and more horrifying to everyone around it.
Trigger Undead Legion Evolution's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks stable unit roles, better corpse conversion, and simple doctrine bonuses for disciplined formations.
Mid progression expands into officer cadres, elite branches, campaign memory, and battlefield adaptation across repeated theaters of war.
Late progression turns the legion into a horrifying war machine whose dead are promoted, specialized, and redeployed with industrial precision.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Necropolis factions court your legion as proof that death can be organized more efficiently than life.
Holy orders mobilize against you because every promotion inside the host is evidence that burial has failed to end service.
The living around you are forced to decide whether your army is a shield against extinction or a desecration that should never be normalized.
questHooks: Reclaim a tomb complex whose ancient dead can either become your elite cadre or awaken as enemies that reject command.
Defend the legion during a holy purge while deciding which settlements you are willing to sacrifice to preserve the host.
Break an internal rebellion sparked by undead officers who have accumulated enough memory to question why they still serve.

name: Revival Bounty Exchange
summary: A grim reward Framework that converts verified revivals, failed hunts, and death-risk contracts into escalating comeback value.
description: Revival Bounty Exchange is a Framework that turns mortal risk and repeated revival into an accumulating reward economy. It belongs in the Framework category because it structures the conversion of death-adjacent events into progression value rather than granting a direct death-cheat in isolation. The bearer gains access to bounties, claims, or escalating payout logic tied to revivals, failed hunts, retaliatory returns, and survivorship accounting. Its progression bias favors audacity, comeback play, and high-risk contracts where most people would never accept the odds. The main tradeoff is predation, because systems that reward returning from death invite enemies, sponsors, and institutions that want to monetize the bearer's suffering. In the world, Revival Bounty Exchange should feel grim and transactional, the kind of framework that war fronts, criminal syndicates, and divine gamblers all find useful for ugly reasons. It should also create ethical instability, since allies may start treating death as an economic event rather than a catastrophe. It remains lore-safe because the Framework pays on events and verified returns, not on free infinite failure, and because every cycle can still accumulate trauma, cost, and retaliation.
coreLoop: Accept or trigger risk-heavy contracts whose payout logic activates only if the bearer returns from verified lethal or near-lethal failure.
Convert revival records into bounty currency, survival clauses, and targeted comeback advantages tailored to the threat that killed you.
Decide whether another payout cycle is worth the growing attention of predators, sponsors, and people pricing your suffering.
Trigger Revival Bounty Exchange's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants modest revival claims, narrow comeback bonuses, and the ability to monetize survival against specific threats.
Mid progression expands into chained bounties, retaliatory contract logic, and specialized clauses that answer repeated causes of death.
Late progression turns the bearer into a notorious death-market asset whose returns are tracked, priced, and exploited across factions.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The more often you come back, the more the world stops seeing a miracle and starts seeing a business model.
Allies may gradually reveal whether they value your life or merely the payout logic that follows your return.
The Framework makes every death a question of who profits, who pays, and whether survival is still yours to define.
questHooks: Survive a contract that promises legendary payout only if you return from a death every patron expects to be permanent.
Expose a betting ring that has started engineering your revivals for profit without your consent.
Choose whether to cash out a life-defining comeback or reject the reward because accepting it would legitimize a monstrous market.

name: Dungeon Farming Loop
summary: A repeat-clear Framework that turns dungeons into optimized extraction loops for leveling, resources, and compounding efficiency.
description: Dungeon Farming Loop is a Framework that organizes dungeons into repeatable extraction, leveling, and refinement cycles. It belongs in the Framework category because it optimizes a progression environment and its outputs rather than granting singular authority over all growth. The bearer learns how to route runs, identify efficient floors, cultivate controlled respawn ecosystems, and compound dungeon yields over time. Its progression bias favors route discipline, resource consistency, and repeatable optimization rather than heroic one-off breakthroughs. The main tradeoff is predictability, because optimized loops invite ambush, burnout, market saturation, and the stagnation that comes from farming what is safe instead of confronting what is transformative. In the world, Dungeon Farming Loop should be economically powerful because stable dungeon extraction can feed guilds, war machines, and entire frontier towns. It should also create political conflict, since monopolizing a dungeon loop is very different from merely clearing a dungeon once. It remains lore-safe because the Framework does not force infinite value into existence, but instead improves how existing dungeon ecosystems are cycled, harvested, and defended.
coreLoop: Map an efficient dungeon route, clear it on repeat, and measure yield in experience, loot, time cost, and environmental strain.
Refine the loop through controlled resets, route discipline, and selective risk-taking that improves output without collapsing the ecosystem.
Decide when to continue compounding safe value and when to break the loop because optimization has started becoming stagnation.
Trigger Dungeon Farming Loop's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth improves route visibility, reset timing, and modest efficiency gains across repeated clears of familiar content.
Mid progression unlocks loop depth bonuses, adaptive route presets, and better handling of ecological backlash from overfarming.
Late progression creates frighteningly efficient extraction engines that can feed entire factions while painting the bearer as a monopolist.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: People living near a profitable loop may depend on your routines even as the dungeon itself starts adapting to being treated like farmland.
What begins as discipline can slowly turn into obsession, especially when safe repetition starts feeling more rational than uncertain growth.
The Framework naturally creates conflict between optimization, ecology, and the human cost of industrialized danger.
questHooks: Break a profitable loop on purpose because the dungeon ecology is beginning to mutate into something the frontier cannot survive.
Win a guild war over access to a route whose repeated clear value is worth more than several border towns.
Choose whether to keep farming the safe path or dive deeper when a rival starts growing faster by risking what you have ignored.

name: Blueprint Forge Library
summary: A crafting Framework that stores, improves, and manufactures schematics so power can scale through reproducible design.
description: Blueprint Forge Library is a Framework that accumulates, organizes, and manufactures power through schematics rather than inspiration alone. It belongs in the Framework category because it structures creation, replication, and scaling across many outputs instead of behaving like one craft cheat. The bearer gains a catalog of blueprints that can be discovered, reverse-engineered, improved, and instantiated through the right facilities and materials. Its progression bias favors preparation, acquisition of patterns, and industrial leverage rather than improvisational raw combat superiority. The main tradeoff is dependency on inputs, because blueprints are only as useful as the materials, tools, labor, and protected space available to realize them. In the world, Blueprint Forge Library should be coveted by states, guilds, and black markets because it threatens artisan monopolies and makes reproducible excellence possible. It should also create intellectual-property conflict in settings where secret designs are part of power, religion, or lineage sovereignty. It remains lore-safe because the Framework still requires legitimate schematics and manufacturable conditions, and because copied or stolen designs can carry flaws, curses, or legal consequences.
coreLoop: Acquire, scan, reverse-engineer, or inherit blueprints and store them in an indexed forge library with quality history attached.
Secure the materials, facilities, and labor needed to produce, refine, or fuse those patterns into real usable outputs.
Scale from isolated craftsmanship into reproducible production while defending your designs from theft, corruption, and sabotage.
Trigger Blueprint Forge Library's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks basic pattern storage, recipe recall, and quality-preserving reproduction of known designs.
Mid progression expands into blueprint fusion, process optimization, and workshop networks that can mass-produce elite equipment.
Late progression makes the bearer an industrial threat whose catalog can shift military balance, trade policy, and sacred manufacturing monopolies.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: A single recovered pattern can change the fate of a city if it enables tools, weapons, or medicines no one else can reliably reproduce.
Every stored design is a future political incident waiting to happen once states and guilds realize what you can manufacture at scale.
The Framework naturally asks whether craft should remain sacred, personal, and rare or become distributable infrastructure.
questHooks: Recover a sacred forge pattern before a state turns it into a weapon platform the original makers would call sacrilege.
Decide whether to publish a medicine blueprint that saves thousands and also destroys the guild that guarded it for centuries.
Stop a counterfeit ring whose flawed copies are killing people while ruining trust in the very designs you spread.

name: Regression Memory Cache
summary: A replay Framework that stores usable residue from failed timelines so future attempts can start with retained knowledge and route leverage.
description: Regression Memory Cache is a Framework that stores the usable residue of failed timelines for later runs. It belongs in the Framework category because it manages information retention and replay leverage rather than directly causing the regression event itself. The bearer gains an indexed cache of lessons, flags, patterns, and partial optimizations harvested from discarded outcomes. Its progression bias favors analysis, selective recall, and gradual route perfection over brute force or dramatic one-time awakenings. The main tradeoff is fragmentation, because memory extracted from failed branches can become incomplete, emotionally distorted, or dangerously overtrusted when context is missing. In the world, Regression Memory Cache should be almost impossible for outsiders to diagnose cleanly, making the bearer appear eerily prepared, paranoid, or prophetic. It should also create inner conflict, since living with the sediment of many failures can make the present feel both precious and unreal. It remains lore-safe because the Cache preserves informational value rather than granting unrestricted dominion over time, and because wrong conclusions from old loops can still kill the bearer in the current branch.
coreLoop: Extract patterns, warnings, and route knowledge from failed timelines, discarded runs, or collapsed branches before they vanish completely.
Index that residue into a cache that can be queried later for tactical hints, decision support, and selective carry-forward leverage.
Use remembered fragments to improve the next attempt while managing the distortion that comes from incomplete and painful evidence.
Trigger Regression Memory Cache's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth improves memory retention, route annotation, and the reliability of small practical hints from failed outcomes.
Mid progression expands cache depth, selective recall, and the ability to preserve more nuanced social or tactical information.
Late progression makes the bearer terrifyingly efficient at iterating solutions, but also increasingly burdened by the emotional sediment of many losses.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: You can feel haunted by tragedies that no one else remembers, which makes every present-tense victory emotionally unstable.
Outsiders may mistake your caution for prophecy when it is really the refined aftermath of repeated failure.
The Framework constantly tests whether your certainty comes from wisdom or from clinging too hard to obsolete branches.
questHooks: Save someone who only dies in branches no one else believes existed and decide how much proof you owe the living.
Destroy a cache shard that contains the perfect tactical answer because keeping it will break what is left of your emotional coherence.
Hunt a rival who has learned how to poison your remembered patterns with false residues from engineered failures.

name: Meta Reincarnation Map
summary: A navigational Framework that reveals rebirth routes, world-line probabilities, and long-view positioning across future lives.
description: Meta Reincarnation Map is a Framework that reveals and organizes the broader structure of world transitions, rebirth routes, and destination logic. It belongs in the Framework category because it provides navigational and structural insight across reincarnation processes rather than acting as a self-sufficient power source. The bearer gains a conceptual map of where souls, lives, roles, and world-lines can lead under specific conditions, making rebirth less blind and more tactical. Its progression bias favors planning across lives, long-view optimization, and intentional identity positioning rather than immediate brute-force gain. The main tradeoff is detachment, because seeing lives as nodes on a map can erode ordinary emotional investment in the current existence. In the world, Meta Reincarnation Map should be treated as blasphemous, sacred, or administratively priceless depending on how local cultures interpret rebirth. It should also create strategic terror, since someone who can navigate future lives intentionally is much harder to permanently defeat. It remains lore-safe because the Map reveals routes and probabilities under existing world law rather than allowing the bearer to invent reincarnation outcomes freely.
coreLoop: Reveal reincarnation routes, future-life vectors, and conditional soul destinations that would otherwise remain hidden after death.
Plan present actions around those routes so the next life, next role, or next world-line begins under better conditions.
Balance long-view optimization against the emotional and moral danger of treating the current life as merely one node in a larger chart.
Trigger Meta Reincarnation Map's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth reveals broad route classes, key transition conditions, and limited previews of likely rebirth outcomes.
Mid progression adds finer branch detail, carry-over positioning, and the ability to recognize sabotage or opportunity across reincarnation chains.
Late progression makes the bearer frighteningly difficult to erase because death becomes a strategic pivot instead of a blind ending.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Framework tempts the bearer to become colder, because every painful present can be rationalized as setup for a better later incarnation.
Religions and bureaucracies built on controlling rebirth have every reason to fear someone carrying an unsanctioned map of the process.
Every choice becomes heavier when you know it may alter not just your fate now, but the shape of several future lives.
questHooks: Choose whether to spend this life opening a better next route or refuse that logic because someone needs you now.
Steal back a reincarnation path that a soul bureaucracy quietly reassigned to a more politically useful candidate.
Break a cult that treats your future-life map as a public resource rather than a burden only you should carry.

name: Time Dilation Training
summary: A training Framework that compresses years of disciplined practice into brief external time without granting free mastery.
description: Time Dilation Training is a Framework that compresses extensive training intervals into externally brief periods. It belongs in the Framework category because it structures growth time and training access rather than granting direct instant mastery on its own. The bearer gains pockets, chambers, or protocol states where effort can be multiplied against outside chronology, allowing years of repetition or study to occur in minutes, hours, or days. Its progression bias favors preparation, discipline, and long-form technique refinement over spontaneous battlefield improvisation. The main tradeoff is isolation, because training too far out of sync with ordinary life can damage relationships, judgment, and the body's ability to reintegrate under real-world pressure. In the world, Time Dilation Training should be one of the most coveted support frameworks because it changes what can be learned before a deadline without necessarily changing what can be survived afterward. It should also remain dangerous because accelerated training magnifies obsession, bad habits, and mental strain along with real progress. It remains lore-safe because all gains are still earned through effort and because compressed time is bounded, resource-gated, and vulnerable to disruption, collapse, or unsustainable overuse.
coreLoop: Enter a valid dilation chamber, ritual pocket, or training protocol where subjective time expands far beyond external chronology.
Spend that expanded interval on real practice, study, conditioning, or controlled experimentation instead of expecting free downloaded mastery.
Re-enter the ordinary world with condensed gains while handling fatigue, disorientation, and the social cost of accelerated personal change.
Trigger Time Dilation Training's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth offers short safe sessions and modest acceleration ratios that improve practice efficiency before major deadlines.
Mid progression expands session length, chamber stability, and the complexity of disciplines that can be trained under dilation.
Late progression lets the bearer prepare at terrifying speed, but only if they can survive the mental and logistical strain of living off-sync.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The bearer can return from a single night carrying the emotional weight of months or years that no one else experienced.
People may admire your impossible improvement pace while never understanding the loneliness and distortion that produced it.
The Framework naturally asks whether mastery gained in isolation still counts when real life keeps moving without you.
questHooks: Survive an emergency training pocket that offers enough time to prepare if it does not break your mind first.
Choose whether to spend your last safe dilation cycle on yourself or on training someone else who might outgrow you.
Keep a collapsing chamber stable long enough to finish the technique that is the only thing standing between your faction and ruin.

name: Inner World Reliquary
summary: A storage and sanctuary Framework that builds a persistent internal world for assets, dependents, and hidden infrastructure.
description: Inner World Reliquary is a Framework that creates a persistent internal space for storing resources, constructs, dependents, and metaphysical infrastructure. It belongs in the Framework category because it is about containment, organization, and scalable internal logistics rather than direct domination of the outside world. The bearer gains an inner domain where goods, armies, relics, cultivation chambers, or spiritual growth structures can be housed, preserved, and managed. Its progression bias favors accumulation, mobility of assets, and hidden preparation rather than immediate transparent power. The main tradeoff is maintenance, because an inner world can decay, rebel, overcrowd, or become a single catastrophic point of failure if neglected or breached. In the world, Inner World Reliquary should be treated as wondrous and terrifying because it collapses logistics, secrecy, and strategic reserve into one body-bound vault. It should also carry existential implications, since people or treasures stored inside another being raise questions about sovereignty, safety, and ownership. It remains lore-safe because internal storage is still bounded by capacity, stability, and breach risk, and because an inner world is not the same thing as independent creation beyond reality's laws.
coreLoop: Expand and stabilize an internal domain that can store resources, structures, dependents, and specialized facilities beyond ordinary carrying capacity.
Use that inner space to preserve value, prepare hidden reserves, and move strategic assets through hostile territory without obvious exposure.
Maintain ecological, political, and spatial order inside the reliquary so convenience does not become concentrated catastrophic risk.
Trigger Inner World Reliquary's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants modest hidden storage, simple sanctuary space, and basic environmental stabilization for important assets.
Mid progression expands the domain into workshops, cultivation sectors, barracks, or dependent habitats with real internal administration needs.
Late progression turns the bearer into a walking logistics empire whose greatest strength and greatest vulnerability occupy the same hidden world.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: What begins as storage can slowly become a society, forcing the bearer to decide whether they are sheltering, ruling, or imprisoning what lives inside.
Every secret reserve inside the reliquary makes the outside world underestimate how much force, wealth, or grief the bearer is carrying.
The Framework makes breaches deeply personal because an attack on the inner world is an attack on everything the bearer chose to protect.
questHooks: Seal a breach before the hidden population inside your reliquary spills into a world that does not know they exist.
Decide which treasure or dependent must be abandoned because the inner world cannot sustain everything you tried to protect.
Survive an invasion by enemies who realize the fastest way to break you is to enter the place you thought was safest.

name: Quest Chain Compounding
summary: A progression Framework that amplifies reward quality when related objectives are linked into coherent escalating chains.
description: Quest Chain Compounding is a Framework that increases reward quality and progression efficiency when related quests are linked into coherent escalating chains. It belongs in the Framework category because it organizes progression flow and payout structure rather than acting as a direct combat or reality-bending power. The bearer becomes exceptionally good at turning one completed objective into the setup for a more valuable next objective, creating momentum through structure instead of through raw personal might. Its progression bias favors planning, continuity, and strategic sequencing over random task completion. The main tradeoff is lock-in, because committing too hard to one chain can blind the bearer to urgent side threats, rival opportunities, or human consequences outside the reward loop. In the world, Quest Chain Compounding should be subtle but potent, especially in settings where institutions, gods, or systems issue tasks that most people treat one at a time. It should also create suspicion because the bearer appears to progress too efficiently through narrative and political complexity, as though the world itself were yielding combo routes. It remains lore-safe because the Framework rewards coherence inside existing objective structures rather than inventing reward-worthy destiny from nothing.
coreLoop: Link one completed objective to the next most synergistic follow-up so effort compounds instead of resetting after every quest turn-in.
Maintain chain continuity through deadlines, branching choices, and controlled escalation to unlock better payouts and strategic momentum.
Decide when to preserve the chain and when to break it because the world is asking for compassion, flexibility, or a different priority.
Trigger Quest Chain Compounding's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth improves chain visibility, follow-up suggestion quality, and modest reward multipliers for coherent quest sequencing.
Mid progression expands into branch-sensitive compounding, campaign-length chains, and reduced loss when one link in the route collapses.
Late progression makes the bearer frighteningly efficient at converting whole arcs of effort into stacked momentum across regions and factions.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Framework can make life feel alarmingly optimized, as if every act of kindness, violence, or diplomacy is one node in a reward lattice.
Rivals may try to interrupt your chains not because they can beat you directly, but because they know breaking momentum is the real attack.
It naturally raises moral questions about whether optimization is helping the world or hollowing out the reasons to act at all.
questHooks: Break a perfect quest chain to save someone the system never marked as reward-relevant and live with what momentum you lose.
Stop a rival compounding route before their optimized campaign hands them a region worth more than any one battlefield victory.
Decide whether to finish the final profitable link or sabotage your own chain because completing it would crown the wrong faction.

name: Reality Edit Interface
summary: A causality-editing Framework that applies bounded local parameter changes and forces the bearer to live with the consequences.
description: Reality Edit Interface is a Framework that exposes a narrow operational layer for editing small local properties of objects, spaces, and interactions. It belongs in the Framework category because it provides a bounded interface and accounting model for changes rather than granting limitless authorship over reality. The bearer can identify editable parameters such as friction, brittleness, pressure, balance, or symbolic state and then spend causality charge to nudge them out of normal alignment. Its progression bias favors precision, preparation, and indirect problem solving instead of overwhelming frontal force. Small edits can produce dramatic outcomes, but only when the bearer understands context well enough to exploit the cascade they are about to start. The main tradeoff is causality stress, because reality resists repeated tampering and begins to charge interest in the form of paradox residue, correction events, and hostile attention. In the world, Reality Edit Interface should feel uncanny and deeply alarming because ordinary witnesses see impossible coincidences while experts realize someone is touching the hidden sliders beneath the surface. It remains lore-safe because edits stay local, expensive, and vulnerable to stronger law, anti-edit fields, or simply the bearer misreading which variable actually matters.
coreLoop: Identify a local parameter that the interface can lawfully expose and decide whether changing it is worth the causality charge.
Apply the edit inside a bounded scope and immediately adapt to the chain reaction it creates in the environment, object, or encounter.
Manage residue, correction pressure, and enemy scrutiny before repeated edits turn a clever exploit into a catastrophic paradox.
Trigger Reality Edit Interface's framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth increases causality charge, improves parameter visibility, and allows safe manipulation of physical properties in a tightly bounded area.
Mid progression unlocks chained edits, environment-level tuning, and carefully limited conceptual adjustments such as fear, luck, or symbolic weight.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying tactician who can unravel stronger foes by touching a few decisive variables at exactly the wrong moment.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: You can engineer disasters that look like coincidence until too many impossible outcomes point back to your hand.
Guardians of time, law, and ritual order hunt you because every edit suggests the world is more editable than they want anyone to know.
The Framework steadily tempts the bearer to treat people and places as parameter sets instead of as lives and histories.
questHooks: Collapse an enemy fortress by finding the one structural or symbolic parameter whose failure will cascade through the whole defense network.
Save a city by editing the wrongness out of a ritual accident before the causality debt rolls forward into mass catastrophe.
Steal a forbidden grammar of edits from a guardian archive that insists no mortal should ever see the world rendered as variables.

name: Dungeon Core Mastery (Living Dungeon System)
summary: A living-dungeon Framework that binds the bearer to a core and turns territorial growth into rooms, monsters, traps, and layered infrastructure.
description: Dungeon Core Mastery is a Framework that fuses the bearer with a dungeon core or an equivalent living control nexus. It belongs in the Framework category because it organizes territorial growth, room logic, spawning, and dungeon infrastructure instead of functioning as a free-floating System usable anywhere. The bearer becomes responsible for shaping an enclosed ecosystem of danger, reward, mana flow, and defensive design. Its progression bias favors territory building, trap architecture, resource routing, and monster curation rather than portable personal supremacy. The dungeon grows as an organism and institution, meaning advancement is measured in complexity, throughput, survivability, and the quality of what the core can sustain. The main tradeoff is immobility and exposure, because the heart of the Framework is tied to a site that enemies can invade, corrupt, starve, or besiege. In the world, Dungeon Core Mastery should be treated as both an economic engine and a strategic threat because a mature living dungeon can shape migration, wealth, frontier survival, and regional war. It remains lore-safe because the Framework is powerful only through managed territory, mana intake, infrastructure, and defendable growth, not through unrestricted authority over the wider world.
coreLoop: Shape rooms, routes, traps, monster ecology, and reward flow so the dungeon grows stronger when intruders engage with it.
Convert mana, harvested resources, and invasion outcomes into structural upgrades, new sectors, and improved core functions.
Defend the heart of the dungeon while deciding whether the territory will become a proving ground, a refuge, a factory, or a predatory maze.
Trigger Dungeon Core Mastery (Living Dungeon System)'s framework protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants simple room templates, low-tier monster spawning, basic trap logic, and enough control to keep the core alive.
Mid progression expands into multi-floor specialization, elite encounters, environmental themes, and internal production or crafting sectors.
Late progression turns the dungeon into a living polity whose economy, defenses, and reputation can influence an entire region.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: People who enter your domain are forced to decide whether they are raiders, pilgrims, workers, or prey, and your layout answers that question for them.
The dungeon slowly becomes a mirror of the bearer's values, whether that means disciplined trial, ecological weirdness, ruthless extraction, or shelter behind teeth.
Every expansion raises the same uncomfortable question: are you building a home, a weapon, or a machine that has already outgrown your right to guide it?
questHooks: Secure a stabilizing heart-material before your core fractures under the stress of recent expansion.
Defeat or absorb a rival living dungeon whose growth model is poisoning the frontier around both your territories.
Use the dungeon itself to shelter a region through disaster while deciding how much danger outsiders must survive to earn that safety.

name: Extra Privilege
summary: A deniable Privilege that grants hidden-route access, buried options, and favorable edge cases inside the world's existing structures.
description: Extra Privilege is a Privilege that grants low-profile access to hidden routes, buried options, and unfairly favorable edge cases in the world's normal decision space. It belongs in the Privilege category because it is precise, asymmetrical, and exception-based rather than a full dominant engine of growth. The bearer does not gain open omniscience or sovereignty, but instead repeatedly notices opportunities that should have remained invisible to ordinary participants. Its progression bias favors subtle play, opportunistic leverage, and selective advantage rather than spectacular direct power. The main tradeoff is exposure, because privileges that rely on remaining deniable become weaker and more dangerous once other actors realize they are being exploited. In the world, Extra Privilege should feel like suspicious luck to outsiders and like a quiet private doorway to the bearer. It should also remain socially volatile, because factions tolerate unfairness better when they cannot prove it than when they can document a pattern. It remains lore-safe because it creates hidden access within existing structures rather than rewriting the structures themselves, and because discovery should trigger countermeasures, audits, or retaliation.
coreLoop: Notice a hidden route, buried option, or favorable edge case that ordinary participants would not realize exists.
Exploit that opening quietly enough to gain leverage, safety, or reward without turning the advantage into public evidence.
Manage exposure so the Privilege stays deniable instead of provoking audits, retaliation, or hard counters.
Trigger Extra Privilege's privilege protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks small hidden choices, side caches, and subtle route deviations that improve survival or reward efficiency.
Mid progression expands into deeper detours, privileged interactions, and more reliable access to low-visibility opportunity windows.
Late progression makes the bearer frighteningly hard to corner, but only if they resist the urge to flaunt every unfair edge they find.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Outsiders experience your success as suspicious luck long before they can explain the pattern behind it.
The Privilege becomes socially dangerous the moment rivals decide your fortune is not fortune at all, but theft from the rules everyone else lives under.
It naturally creates tension between careful survival and the temptation to abuse every hidden opening while you still can.
questHooks: Use a hidden route to save someone from a doomed scene without revealing how you knew the route existed at all.
Erase evidence of repeated favorable outcomes before a rival faction proves your luck is a pattern worth killing over.
Choose whether to expose one secret edge publicly because silence would protect you and doom everyone else.

name: Class Unique Covenant
summary: A singular-class Privilege that binds the bearer to a one-of-one class line no ordinary claimant may legally or metaphysically hold.
description: Class Unique Covenant is a Privilege that binds the bearer to a one-of-one class path unavailable to ordinary claimants. It belongs in the Privilege category because it is a narrow entitlement to exclusivity, not a complete replacement for every other progression rule. The bearer receives a protected class identity with unique skills, sigils, and inheritance rights that cannot be copied or normally stolen. Its progression bias favors defending legitimacy, proving worth, and deepening a singular lane instead of broad system-level dominance. The main tradeoff is visibility, because a unique class becomes a beacon for challengers, thieves, guilds, and institutions that want to regulate or possess it. In the world, Class Unique Covenant should be treated as a living seal of status and danger, especially in cultures where classes define social hierarchy as much as combat role. It should also create pressure of expectation, since every failure by the bearer can be interpreted as a failure of the covenant's supposed singular worth. It remains lore-safe because uniqueness is still bounded to one class line and one inheritance channel, and because challengers, oathbreaks, or covenant decay can still threaten it.
coreLoop: Claim or preserve a one-of-one class line through covenant trials, legitimacy checks, and protected inheritance rights.
Deepen that singular class through sigils, exclusive techniques, and covenant-recognized class milestones.
Defend the covenant from challengers, thieves, and institutions that want to break, regulate, or possess what only you may hold.
Trigger Class Unique Covenant's privilege protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth establishes legitimacy, unlocks the first exclusive class features, and proves the bearer can survive public scrutiny.
Mid progression expands into sigil inheritance, anti-theft protections, and deeper one-lineage specialization.
Late progression turns the class into a political and metaphysical issue, because its sole bearer becomes the only gateway to its future.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: People do not merely judge your strength; they judge whether you deserve a privilege no one else was allowed to receive.
Every challenger can frame themselves as either a usurper or the rightful correction to a covenant the world thinks was misbestowed.
The Privilege naturally creates identity pressure because losing faith in the class can start looking like covenant decay rather than ordinary doubt.
questHooks: Defeat a covenant challenger who might honestly deserve the class more than you do and decide what legitimacy means afterward.
Recover a lost sigil that proves your claim before a guild court brands your covenant fraudulent.
Choose whether to let the class die with you or rewrite the covenant so someone else can inherit what was meant to remain singular.

name: Information Vision Array
summary: A scan-focused Privilege that reveals bounded layers of stats, weaknesses, hidden routes, and structural truth beyond ordinary perception.
description: Information Vision Array is a Privilege that reveals targeted layers of stats, weakness data, hidden routes, and structural insight beyond normal perception. It belongs in the Privilege category because it grants a narrow but highly efficient information advantage rather than governing the entire world's knowledge flow. The bearer can scan a target, site, or object and surface the specific details that matter most for survival, exploitation, or strategic planning. Its progression bias favors preparation, clean execution, and low-waste decision making instead of blind improvisation. The main tradeoff is interpretation burden, because more visible information does not automatically produce better judgment and can overwhelm or mislead under pressure. In the world, Information Vision Array should feel uncanny because the bearer appears to know more than they should about guarded things, hidden flaws, and concealed pathways. It should also attract resistance from secret-keepers, illusionists, and factions whose power depends on information asymmetry. It remains lore-safe because it reveals patterned truth within bounded scans instead of granting total knowledge, and because strong concealment, false data, and higher law can still interfere.
coreLoop: Scan a target, object, or environment to surface the most actionable hidden data available within the Arrays current limits.
Interpret that data fast enough to turn knowledge into cleaner tactics, route choices, or survival decisions.
Manage scan cost, concealment resistance, and information overload so insight remains useful instead of destabilizing.
Trigger Information Vision Array's privilege protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth reveals basic weaknesses, route indicators, and quality or danger tags on scanned targets and spaces.
Mid progression expands scan depth, predictive overlays, and better distinction between true signals and false or planted data.
Late progression makes the bearer terrifyingly efficient at preparation, but only if they can still judge what matters under pressure.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Array turns secrecy itself into a contested battlefield, because any faction living on hidden truth starts treating you as a threat.
People often mistake the Privilege for impossible genius, which creates both awe and fear around your choices.
It naturally raises the question of whether seeing more truth makes someone wiser or simply harder to deceive.
questHooks: Scan a sacred relic that everyone reveres and decide whether exposing its hidden flaw will save lives or start a war.
Map a concealed route through a zone layered with deliberate false signals designed to kill overconfident analysts.
Choose whether to reveal what you saw in an ally's sealed gear when sharing that truth could shatter the trust holding your group together.

name: Mind-Reading Exploit
summary: A taboo Privilege that exposes surface intent and decision pressure in crucial moments without granting total mental domination.
description: Mind-Reading Exploit is a Privilege that surfaces intent, surface thought, or immediate decision pressure at crucial moments. It belongs in the Privilege category because it offers an unfair angle on cognition without becoming total psychic domination. The bearer does not own minds, but can exploit brief windows of readability to predict movement, expose lies, and understand motive faster than ordinary intuition should allow. Its progression bias favors duels, negotiations, and high-tension social moments where one glimpse of intent changes everything. The main tradeoff is social poison, because being able to read too much too often destabilizes trust and can isolate the bearer from ordinary intimacy. In the world, Mind-Reading Exploit should feel invasive and taboo even when used for good reasons, since very few cultures remain comfortable around someone who can peel back intent. It should also meet natural counters such as trained discipline, mind shields, contradictory self-belief, and creatures whose thought patterns are not humanly legible. It remains lore-safe because it is a short-window exploit of readable cognition, not unrestricted ownership of consciousness, and because misuse should invite psychic backlash, paranoia, or retaliation.
coreLoop: Catch a brief readable window in an enemy, ally, or target mind during stress, decision pressure, or focused attention.
Turn that glimpse of surface intent into better timing, cleaner dialogue leverage, or sharper prediction of immediate action.
Avoid overuse and social fallout so the Privilege remains an edge instead of becoming the reason no one trusts you.
Trigger Mind-Reading Exploit's privilege protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth improves the clarity of short intent flashes during obvious stress or combat commitment windows.
Mid progression expands into negotiation pressure reads, lie detection support, and stronger resistance against basic mental noise.
Late progression makes the bearer terrifying in duels and tense conversations, but also increasingly alien in ordinary relationships.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Privilege turns honesty into a complicated concept because you can hear thoughts people never meant to make into speech.
Even justified use can leave the bearer socially isolated, since very few people feel safe around someone who reads what should remain private.
It naturally creates scenes where the truth is not comforting, only actionable.
questHooks: Catch the one surface thought that reveals an assassination plan before the speaker commits to silence forever.
Win a negotiation by reading intent at the exact moment it fractures, then decide whether anyone involved can still trust you afterward.
Face an enemy whose contradictory beliefs make every read dangerous because the wrong surface thought is the bait, not the truth.

name: Villain POV Advantage
summary: A morally unstable Privilege that unlocks ruthless options, intimidation leverage, and antagonist-style strategic framing others resist using.
description: Villain POV Advantage is a Privilege that grants access to ruthless options, intimidation leverage, and antagonistic strategic framing that ordinary protagonists hesitate to use. It belongs in the Privilege category because it is a narrative-position advantage and a menu of efficient exceptions, not a complete dark System. The bearer sees how resource seizure, fear, hostage logic, timing cruelty, and asymmetrical escalation can solve problems that heroic conventions leave open. Its progression bias favors pressure, deterrence, and exploitation of enemy hesitation rather than broad lawful legitimacy. The main tradeoff is reputation, because every efficient villain-coded choice compounds suspicion, infamy, and organized opposition even when it works. In the world, Villain POV Advantage should feel like seeing the same board from the side of people who stop asking permission. It should also remain morally unstable, because the advantage often comes from recognizing practical routes that are effective precisely because decent people resist using them. It remains lore-safe because it does not grant automatic victory, only access to darker strategic options and stronger returns on fear, coercion, and disruption.
coreLoop: Recognize a ruthless option that heroic or lawful framing would normally leave off the table.
Use intimidation, disruption, coercion, or resource seizure to solve the problem faster than cleaner methods would allow.
Pay the resulting social and narrative debt as infamy, retaliation, and legitimacy erosion accumulate around you.
Trigger Villain POV Advantage's privilege protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks minor intimidation routes, coercive leverage, and low-tier gains from fear-based pressure.
Mid progression expands into infamy-driven perks, stronger disruption options, and more efficient exploitation of enemy hesitation.
Late progression makes the bearer frighteningly effective in crisis, but also increasingly defined by the enemies and debts their methods create.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Privilege constantly asks whether efficiency is courage, corruption, or simply the first step toward becoming what you hate.
People may admire your results while privately fearing the logic you used to achieve them.
Every darkly practical victory makes later mercy harder to prove.
questHooks: Seize a resource the hero faction refuses to touch and decide whether the resulting victory was worth becoming the story's villain in public.
Break an enemy coalition through fear and coercion before it matures into war, then face what your allies think you became to do it.
Reject the clean efficient option once and watch the Privilege punish you by showing exactly how many lives the darker route would have saved.

name: Danger Sense Array
summary: A survival Privilege that flags lethal intent and incoming disaster moments before ordinary perception can fully respond.
description: Danger Sense Array is a Privilege that flags imminent lethal threats before ordinary perception can fully register them. It belongs in the Privilege category because it is a narrow survival exception, not a complete combat system or dominion power. The bearer receives warnings, intuition spikes, or microsecond predictive flashes that allow evasive action in moments where everyone else would already be dead. Its progression bias favors survival, counter-ambush play, and risk management rather than direct offensive escalation. The main tradeoff is false confidence, because sensing danger does not guarantee the body, positioning, or resources needed to escape it cleanly. In the world, Danger Sense Array should make the bearer infuriating to assassins, fate-readers, and ambush specialists who rely on surprise maintaining absolute value. It should also create tension with allies, because people may start relying on the bearer to sense what no normal scout could have caught in time. It remains lore-safe because it warns of danger rather than preventing it outright, and because saturation, misdirection, void-noise, or overwhelming area threats can still break through.
coreLoop: Catch warning spikes just before a lethal strike, trap, or disaster fully resolves into unavoidable harm.
Spend that narrow window on evasion, counterplay, triage, or choosing which danger matters most right now.
Avoid mistaking warning for safety, because the Privilege only buys reaction time, not guaranteed survival.
Trigger Danger Sense Array's privilege protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants brief warning flashes against obvious lethal intent, ambushes, and immediate physical threats.
Mid progression expands the warning window, threat classification, and the ability to distinguish false signals from true kill pressure.
Late progression makes the bearer maddeningly hard to surprise, but still vulnerable to saturation, area denial, and impossible positioning.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Array makes ordinary safety feel temporary, because the world keeps revealing how many ways death was already on its way.
Allies may become dangerously dependent on the bearer's warnings instead of learning to read danger for themselves.
Assassins and fate-readers hate what they cannot cleanly surprise.
questHooks: Survive an assassination chain by acting on warnings too fast for anyone else to understand what nearly happened.
Choose who to save when the Array fires for two lethal threats at once and your body can only answer one in time.
Calibrate the Privilege inside a void-noise storm where every warning could be true, false, or intentionally poisoned.

name: Instant Comprehension Grant
summary: A rapid-learning Privilege that collapses exposure into functional understanding for bounded concepts, techniques, and texts.
description: Instant Comprehension Grant is a Privilege that collapses the delay between exposure and functional understanding for highly specific concepts, techniques, and texts. It belongs in the Privilege category because it is a potent exception to normal learning friction, but still narrower and less identity-defining than a full knowledge-oriented System. The bearer can encounter a law, language, form, or mechanism and grasp its essentials with impossible speed. Its progression bias favors rapid adaptation, curiosity, and opportunistic learning under pressure rather than slow institutional study. The main tradeoff is embodiment lag, because understanding a thing is not the same as having the body, resources, or context to execute it safely at full depth. In the world, Instant Comprehension Grant should inspire admiration and fear because it undermines every hierarchy built on exclusive learning and long initiation. It should also provoke hoarding behavior from institutions that realize their secrets can be absorbed from one brief encounter. It remains lore-safe because the Privilege accelerates comprehension within contact and conceptual limits rather than granting automatic mastery of every truth in existence.
coreLoop: Encounter a technique, language, law, or mechanism and trigger a rapid comprehension event while the concept is still in reach.
Convert that sudden understanding into immediate utility, translation, or tactical adaptation before the opportunity passes.
Deal with the gap between knowing and embodying, because insight arrives faster than the body, resources, or context needed to wield it well.
Trigger Instant Comprehension Grant's privilege protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants rapid understanding of texts, simple techniques, and clearly structured mechanisms after direct exposure.
Mid progression expands into more abstract concepts, faster integration, and better retention under stress or incomplete contact.
Late progression makes the bearer terrifyingly quick to learn, but still unable to skip the hard work of embodiment and context.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Privilege makes teachers, libraries, and guarded traditions nervous because centuries of gatekeeping can collapse in one encounter.
Rapid understanding can become isolating when the bearer begins leaping over learning journeys that once defined whole communities.
It naturally creates scenes where genius arrives before wisdom, and that difference matters.
questHooks: Grasp a forbidden manual fast enough to survive the scene, then decide whether keeping that understanding is worth who it will draw to you.
Translate a dead language before the ruin collapses even though true mastery of what you read may take years you do not have.
Choose whether to teach what you suddenly learned or hide it because the people who guarded it will kill to keep the old hierarchy intact.

name: Glitch Exploit Overlay
summary: An instability-driven Overlay that abuses cracks, timing faults, and unintended rule gaps for temporary advantage at escalating risk.
description: Glitch Exploit Overlay is an Overlay that reveals and weaponizes cracks, timing faults, and unintended edge cases in the world's normal operating rules. It belongs in the Overlay category because it does not own law the way an Authority does or organize progression the way a Framework does, but instead rides on top of existing structures and abuses their instability. The bearer sees moments where systems can be clipped, delayed, duplicated, bypassed, or desynchronized for temporary advantage. Its progression bias favors improvisation, opportunism, and calculated abuse of unstable windows rather than clean repeatable mastery. The main tradeoff is backlash, because every exploit deepens instability, increases detection risk, and makes future failures more catastrophic if the world starts correcting around the bearer. In the world, Glitch Exploit Overlay should feel profoundly wrong even to people who do not understand it, as though causality and interface etiquette are being violated at the edges. It should also attract hunters, auditors, and cosmic immune responses that exist specifically to patch anomalies before they spread. It remains lore-safe because the Overlay never truly supersedes deeper law; it only distorts local behavior temporarily, and stronger structures can still collapse or punish the exploit.
coreLoop: Identify a crack, timing fault, or misaligned rule interaction in the current situation before the world fully corrects it.
Spend that exploit window on a temporary bypass, duplication, desync, or illegal movement the base rules should not have allowed.
Manage instability and detection so the gain from one exploit does not trigger catastrophic correction before the next choice matters.
Trigger Glitch Exploit Overlay's overlay protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth reveals basic exploit windows and grants narrow rule-bending bursts that can save the bearer in sharp moments.
Mid progression expands into chained abuse patterns, stronger anomaly literacy, and better handling of correction backlash.
Late progression makes the bearer terrifyingly slippery, but only so long as the world has not fully decided to patch them out.

narrativeHooks: The Overlay makes even ordinary victories feel stolen, because success arrives through seams the world clearly wanted closed.
Auditors, enforcers, and system cults treat the bearer less like a criminal and more like a contagious breach.

questHooks: Use a forbidden exploit to stop an execution, then outrun the enforcers who know a correction wave is already building around you.
Break into a sealed zone by clipping through a fault in its law and discover why the fault existed in the first place.
Choose whether to trigger a city-wide bypass that saves thousands now but may teach the world to patch over all future mercy routes.

name: Rollback Overlay
summary: A desperate Overlay that steals a tiny slice of recent reality back after harm, at the cost of strain and temporal contamination.
description: Rollback Overlay is an Overlay that permits the bearer to revert an extremely small slice of recent reality after a harmful outcome. It belongs in the Overlay category because it is a desperate exploit layered over normal causality rather than a legitimate time System or Framework. The bearer does not rewind lives, timelines, or whole scenes, but instead steals a few moments back from finalized action to correct a misstep, dodge a strike, or alter a decision window. Its progression bias favors clutch survival, precision, and extreme pressure response over long-term stable planning. The main tradeoff is strain, because each rollback scrapes against already-committed reality and should accumulate disorientation, paradox residue, or local instability. In the world, Rollback Overlay should be nearly impossible to prove but terrifying to suspect, especially for duelists, assassins, and enforcers who know they landed the killing blow. It should also remain visibly unhealthy for the bearer, since repeated micro-reversions should create flicker, nausea, memory splitting, or existential slippage. It remains lore-safe because it exploits a tiny local seam in event finalization rather than granting true sovereign control over time, and because deeper law can jam, punish, or refuse the rollback.
coreLoop: Suffer or detect a harmful outcome severe enough to justify spending a tiny rollback window on immediate correction.
Revert only the most recent actionable slice of local reality and use that stolen second chance for a better response.
Absorb the strain, residue, and disorientation that follow every attempt to peel finalized events back off the world.
Trigger Rollback Overlay's overlay protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants one-beat reversals that can save the bearer from a single bad dodge, strike, or spoken mistake.
Mid progression expands rollback precision, residue tolerance, and the ability to preserve coherence across repeated clutch corrections.
Late progression makes the bearer horrifying in close pressure situations, but increasingly unstable everywhere else.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Enemies who should have won start doubting their senses, which makes the bearer feel more uncanny with every impossible survival.
The Overlay turns regret into a tactical resource, but also a psychological poison, because every saved second reminds you what nearly happened.
It naturally creates scenes where reality itself seems reluctant to admit what just occurred.
questHooks: Survive a duel no one believes you could have survived and decide whether proving the truth is worth revealing the exploit.
Use the last safe rollback charge to save an ally, knowing the next correction may tear your memory apart.
Track down the thing in reality that keeps jamming your reversions before one failed rollback becomes permanent death.

name: Phantom Inventory Overlay
summary: An unstable storage Overlay that hides contraband and emergency assets in illegal slots outside normal inventory accounting.
description: Phantom Inventory Overlay is an Overlay that creates unstable hidden storage slots outside normal inventory accounting. It belongs in the Overlay category because it piggybacks on item-state logic and creates illegal storage behavior instead of granting a lawful storage domain like a Framework would. The bearer can tuck items into inaccessible, partially real inventory spaces that bypass weight, seals, inspections, or slot rules for limited periods. Its progression bias favors smuggling, emergency reserve play, and impossible preparedness rather than honorable transparent logistics. The main tradeoff is loss risk, because phantom slots should drift, corrupt, or collapse unpredictably when overloaded or observed too closely. In the world, Phantom Inventory Overlay should be the nightmare of quartermasters, jailers, customs officers, and thieves because it breaks the assumptions that make item control possible. It should also feel spiritually suspect, as if objects placed into these slots are only half guaranteed to return in the same state. It remains lore-safe because the storage is unstable and parasitic on existing item logic, not a true self-owned pocket world, and because audits, null fields, or instability spikes can eject or erase what is hidden there.
coreLoop: Slip an item into an illegal phantom slot that temporarily bypasses normal inventory, weight, seal, or inspection logic.
Hold that hidden asset only as long as the slot remains coherent enough to retrieve it without collapse or corruption.
Choose when the risk of keeping contraband hidden is greater than the risk of pulling it back into lawful space.
Trigger Phantom Inventory Overlay's overlay protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants a few unstable hidden slots suitable for contraband, emergency consumables, or small illicit tools.
Mid progression improves slot coherence, retrieval reliability, and the ability to hold stranger or heavier objects briefly.
Late progression makes the bearer terrifyingly prepared, but only if they can live with the constant fear that the wrong item may vanish forever.

narrativeHooks: Every hidden slot turns the simple act of carrying something into a low-grade horror about whether the item still exists correctly.
The Overlay makes authorities paranoid because it breaks every assumption that keeps prisons, customs, and vault inspections meaningful.
It naturally creates scenes where trust in your own reserves becomes as fragile as trust in the world around you.
questHooks: Smuggle a relic through an inspection regime so severe that failure means the slot, the item, and possibly your hand all vanish together.
Break someone out of prison using tools hidden in phantom slots you are no longer sure can still return cleanly.
Choose whether to keep a cursed object hidden a little longer or pull it out now before the slot mutates it into something worse.

name: Null Cost Overlay
summary: A debt-heavy Overlay that suppresses apparent activation cost in the moment and makes reality collect payment later with interest.
description: Null Cost Overlay is an Overlay that intermittently suppresses the normal cost of abilities, movement, or activation at the moment of use. It belongs in the Overlay category because it is a temporary exploit of accounting logic rather than a lawful increase in reserves, regeneration, or authority. The bearer can force a skill, cast, or maneuver through with zero apparent payment, slipping past the usual cost check before reality catches up. Its progression bias favors burst turns, illegal combos, and impossible action chains rather than sustainable throughput. The main tradeoff is deferred debt, because costs denied in the moment should return later as backlash, exhaustion spikes, broken channels, or attracted enforcement. In the world, Null Cost Overlay should appear as impossible efficiency and therefore immediately alarm anyone who understands resource discipline. It should also provoke envy and fear, since every trained fighter knows how much power depends on what cannot normally be done for free. It remains lore-safe because the cost is not truly erased, only displaced, and because the ledger of reality should always demand settlement eventually.
coreLoop: Trigger an action that should cost more than you can presently afford and force it through by nulling the immediate payment check.
